classes.description: This course is for amateur singers who may sing in a church choir, community chorus, or community musical theatre troupe, who are not new to choral singing, yet want a fun way to enhance their ear and eye training in reading a musical score. Developing a few skills will make learning parts quicker and easier! We will work on fun and practical ways to improve music reading skills using Broadway, folk, hymn tunes, and choral music. Musicians with instrumental background who wish to hone their sight singing skills are also welcome!

classes.title: Sight Singing for Adults
classes.description: This course is for amateur singers who may sing in a church choir, community chorus, or community musical theatre troupe, who are not new to choral singing, yet want a fun way to enhance their ear and eye training in reading a musical score. Developing a few skills will make learning parts quicker and easier! We will work on fun and practical ways to improve music reading skills using Broadway, folk, hymn tunes, and choral music. Musicians with instrumental background who wish to hone their sight singing skills are also welcome!

classes.title: Ukulele and You
classes.description: In one week, you will get the basics of playing chords to various styles of music such as folk, classic rock, and blues. Whether or not you have studied music before, ukulele is the best starting place for understanding and ENJOYING the world of music making. Playing with a class is the quickest way to learn and like how you sound! This class helps intermediate players learn more repertoire and improve strumming skills. You may borrow a CHQ Uke for the week or bring your own.

classes.title: Guitar Play and Sing Along
classes.description: This class will provide a springboard for learning how to play guitar and sing with others. Participants can expect to gain a good understanding and appreciation of folk, rock, country and popular songs from the past. Special consideration will be given to the favorite songs of the participants. We will explore guitar chords for songs in three different keys. The ability to read music is not required, as we will be learning not from an academic point but from the heart.

classes.title: Classical Music Lab, Fun and Games for Lifelong Learners: Tuesday Session
classes.description: Ignite your Artistic Intelligence through classical music! This fun hands-on exploration with Steinway Artist and former university faculty Hsing-ay Hsu brings you a buffet of Conscious Listening™ activities on different music each day: Phrasing Movement Meditation, Drawing Melodies, Musical Characters, Comparing Styles, Humming for Health, Piano Improv for Everyone, Favorite Songs Show & Tell. Instruments welcome. This single day course is being offered on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.

classes.title: Classical Music Lab, Fun and Games for Lifelong Learners: Tuesday Session
classes.description: Ignite your Artistic Intelligence through classical music! This fun hands-on exploration with Steinway Artist and former university faculty Hsing-ay Hsu brings you a buffet of Conscious Listening™ activities on different music each day: Phrasing Movement Meditation, Drawing Melodies, Musical Characters, Comparing Styles, Humming for Health, Piano Improv for Everyone, Favorite Songs Show & Tell. Instruments welcome. This single day course is being offered on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.

This fun hands-on exploration with Steinway Artist and former university faculty Hsing-ay Hsu brings you a buffet of Conscious Listening™ activities on different music each day: Phrasing Movement Meditation, Drawing Melodies, Musical Characters, Comparing Styles, Humming for Health, Piano Improv for Everyone, Favorite Songs Show & Tell. Instruments welcome. This single day course is being offered on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.

classes.title: Drumming for Connection: Exploring Emotional Awareness Through Rhythm
classes.description: Join Chautauqua Institution Director of Arts Education Suzanne Fassett-Wright for an energetic, hands-on introduction to "Feelin' the Beat," a drumming program that blends music-making with social–emotional learning. You'll try sample activities, explore how musical expression supports teamwork, emotional awareness, and self-regulation, and experience the power of arts-integrated learning firsthand. Drums provided.

classes.title: Learn to Play Guitar
classes.description: Guitar basics in one week! While this course is designed for beginners, players with some experience playing guitar will acquire new information and be challenged. We will cover chords in three keys and work on strumming in different styles while we play folk, country, blues, and rock tunes. Students will also learn to play melodies using Tab. The best thing about taking group lessons is that someone is always playing the correct notes or chords at the correct time, so students learn more quickly and with confidence. You may borrow a Chautauqua guitar for the week or bring your own.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: Music as Voyage Shared Listening with Del Sol Quartet
classes.description: Join Del Sol Quartet to discuss ways that music can gather us together to listen, share, and explore. Our starting place will be Leilehua Lanzilotti's new composition, Moananuiaˉkea, commissioned to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the launch of Hokule'a, an iconic Hawaiian voyaging canoe.

classes.title: Introduction to Japanese
classes.description: Students will be introduced to the basics of learning Japanese. Course content will include how to read hiragana, how to pronounce Japanese words, and basic words and phrases that are useful for tourists.

classes.title: Signed Language, Culture, and Connection: An Introduction to the Deaf Community
classes.description: Step into the vibrant world of Deaf culture and American Sign Language (ASL) in this immersive one-week workshop. Participants will discover how language, culture, and community come alive through visual communication while gaining hands-on experience with everyday ASL signs and expressive strategies. Through interactive activities, storytelling, and guided practice, this course invites curiosity, connection, and a deeper appreciation for Deaf ways of being, no prior experience required.

classes.title: French Language Learning for Families
classes.description: This family-friendly course offers a fun and engaging introduction to the French language. Children and their adult family members: parents, guardians, or grandparents, will explore French-speaking regions while learning vocabulary related to art, weather, geography, emotions, clothing, food, and basic conversation. Beginners are welcome, and all activities are designed to support shared family learning and confidence together. Parents and children are particularly encouraged to attend together.

classes.title: French for Fun and Travel
classes.description: Traveling to a French speaking country? Want to increase your neuronal activity? Do you simply think that French is a beautiful language? Whatever the reason, you will learn basic French phrases. The focus will be on both listening and speaking activities, with cultural asides in a low-pressure environment. This course is for beginners or those with little to no experience with the language.

classes.title: Introduction to American Sign Language
classes.description: This is an introductory class into American Sign Language (ASL), the third most commonly used language in the United States. It will cover the basics of common phrases, fingerspelling, and a bit about the linguistics of this language.

classes.title: Latin Laid Bare: Latin 101
classes.description: Whether a novice or a former student, you'll be surprised at how much of the basic language you can encounter in just five sessions. This systematic approach covers both the structure of Latin and its effect upon English through vocabulary. This is Latin for the curious, not Latin for dummies, and taught by an instructor with forty years' experience. Each session includes a translation and discussion of an extract from a Roman author, introducing its context and significance. These include Catullus (love poetry), Caesar (history/propaganda), Horace (satire), Vergil (epic), & Pliny (letters).

classes.title: Italiano pronti e via: Italian Culture & Conversational Phrases
classes.description: Traveling to Italy or just interested in Italian culture and some conversational phrases? Federica will be delighted to walk and talk with you on an imaginary journey to Italy. No previous experience in Italian is necessary.

classes.title: It's All Greek to Me: The Ancient Language '101'
classes.description: This course examines the sight, sounds and syntax of classical Greek. Learn the story behind the alphabet, encounter the grammar and structure of the language, and explore numerous Greek derivatives used in both everyday and scientific English. Greek was the language of poets and philosophers, doctors and demagogues; what is it about this language that made it so versatile? Each session includes an extract from an ancient Greek author, introducing its context and significance. These include Homer (epic), Herodotus (history), Sophocles (tragedy), Aristophanes (comedy) and Plato (philosophy).

classes.title: Seeds of Change: Lessons from Octavia Butler's Parables
classes.description: In a world unraveling under the weight of climate chaos, social fragmentation, and political upheaval, Octavia Butler's Parable of the Sower and Parable of the Talents offer a prophetic lens on resilience, leadership, and hope. In this four-session course, you will examine themes of justice and community, explore how prophetic storytelling speaks to today's challenges, and expand your ability to shape a future rooted in adaptability, compassion, and purpose.

classes.title: Capturing Lives: Fiction Vs. Nonfiction
classes.description: What choices do authors make when they set out to tell the story of a person's life? The instructor, the author of both a novel and a traditional biography about Emily Hale, the long-time secret love of the poet T. S. Eliot, reviews the choices she and other authors have made in telling the story of lives for whom the record is incomplete. The class will address issues that may be faced by persons wanting to capture the stories of their family members.

classes.title: Saturday Morning Short Story Discussion Group
classes.description: The short story, a 180-year-old genre, has works of great power and resonance. Students read a different short story for each week. There will be guided discussions of the stories, using Socratic questioning techniques so that each student will emerge with an enriched reading of the story. Discussion participants must read the assigned story before attending the class. Each story will be available at the Smith Memorial Library circulation desk one week before the class, or students can email the instructor at markernalt21@yahoo.com.

classes.title: Tintin: Childhood Hero or Political Pawn
classes.description: Have you ever read one of the TINTIN adventure comic books? We will look at one particular early adventure: TINTIN EN AMÉRIQUE as it is particularly relevant to many of us: Prohibition, western expansionism, mafia intrusion etc. We will compare and contrast the original French as well as the English translation. We will also delve into the author, HERGÉ's somewhat checkered past, and see how that may have influenced the way that Tintin was used as a geopolitical lens. A knowledge of French is ideal but not necessary.

classes.title: Reading and Discussion: Stories with Musical Themes
classes.description: Each day will study a different short story with a musical theme. Students will discuss and learn how understanding the music reference in each story enhance the story's meaning.

classes.title: Weekday Short Story Discussion Group
classes.description: Students will read the assigned story for each class and engage in an open inquiry (Socratic) discussion of the story during class. The goal is to interact with the text, other readers, and leave with an enriched reading of the story. Five stories will be read and discussed. Stories will be distributed at the first class. This class meets daily for one week. If you are interested in registering for the single day workshop, register for "Saturday Morning Short Story Discussion Group".

classes.title: Masterpiece Authors: Shakespeare and Twain
classes.description: In both British and American literature, countless authors have shaped the literary landscape, yet two figures stand out as enduring masters of their craft: William Shakespeare and Mark Twain. Through works such as Shakespeare's Hamlet and Twain's Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, readers encounter timeless explorations of human psychology, society, and moral complexity. Studying the authors' biographies, examining critical interpretations, and engaging closely with their most influential texts deepens one's appreciation and understanding, offering a challenging and rewarding journey into the heart of classic literature.

classes.title: Anna Karenina: Love, Morality, and Meaning in Tolstoy's Masterpiece
classes.description: Leo Tolstoy's Anna Karenina remains one of the most psychologically rich and philosophically provocative novels ever written. Its opening line, "All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way" invites readers into a world of passionate love, moral conflict, social pressure, and the universal human search for meaning. This one-week seminar invites participants to revisit (or encounter for the first time) Tolstoy's novel in an intimate, intellectually vibrant setting. Each session blends close reading, historical context, discussion, and a guided reflection.

classes.title: The Literary Geography of Japan
classes.description: This course introduces major works of Japanese literature available in English translation where the physical environment, both natural and built, plays a central role. The instructor will introduce works set in a particular region and in which landscape plays a central role. We'll read short passages from each describing a specific place and then look at those places today, emphasizing ways that the ghosts of former landscapes can still be found in 21st century Japan.

classes.title: Shakespeare's Sonnets: Poetry and Play
classes.description: We think of sonnets mainly as love poems, but they were also a way of competing creatively. In Shakespeare's day, people would circulate sonnets, challenging each other to contests of wit. With the structural complexity of Bach, and Mozart's playfulness, their appeal has continued well into the 21st century, through W.B. Yeats, Robert Frost, Gwendolyn Brooks, and Tracy K. Smith. This discussion-based course will look at wide-ranging examples of the form, and the innovations made by poets fascinated by the sonnet's creative potential.

classes.title: Short Stories and Drama of Anton Chekhov: An Introduction
classes.description: Short course on the Russian master of the short story and drama. Discussion will depart from four central themes: what is special about Russian literature; what Chekhov's tales reveal about his time and milieu, and what we in turn need to know about that context to understand his stories; what is distinctive about the doctor-writer Chekhov and which analytical techniques are most useful in interpreting his works; and how he connects to us today.

classes.title: History of Science Fiction and Its Impact on Society
classes.description: Sci-Fi is unique among literary genres both a mirror of society and a driver of change. From early mythic tales and Gulliver's Travels to Shelley's Frankenstein and the visionary works of Verne and H.G. Wells, science fiction has reflected humanity's hopes, fears, and imagination. This course traces the evolution of Sci-Fi in literature, film, and TV, examining how it has inspired innovation, shaped politics, culture, and influenced how we envision the future. Each session includes discussion, clips, and readings that reveal how sci-fi not only entertains but transform the way we see the world.

classes.title: Shakespeare and Social Justice
classes.description: Social justice themes run throughout Shakespeare's work. We place faith in legal and religious texts to envision equity, but Shakespeare's plays show us gaps in our efforts, often in places where we aren't looking. We'll take a deep dive into two plays: The Merchant of Venice and A Midsummer Night's Dream, examining competing perspectives in social institutions such as the law, the economy, and marriage, and how they shape the social worlds we inhabit.

classes.title: Twelve Angry Men: A study in American citizenship
classes.description: This story, originally a 1954 teleplay for CBS's Studio One, was adapted into a stage play and first performed in 1955 and became a major motion picture in 1957. We will examine it theatrically and as literature to understand its view of the American legal system and how Democracy informs laws to promise a fair trial to all. Mark Altschuler (college English teacher) and Stephen Stout (actor, director and theatre teacher) have found a way to explore written theatrical works as both literature and performance. This collaboration has led to a style of teaching that creates room for all interpretations while learning about plays from two frames of reference.

classes.title: So You Want to Get Published
classes.description: Writing a book can be very satisfying, but seeing a manuscript through to publication and into the hands of readers can turn into a challenge. The instructor, a multi-published author of both fiction and non-fiction, reviews the process from start to finish, addressing these and other questions from her own experiences and those of other authors: How do I find an agent? Do I need one? How do I find a publisher? What are the unexpected costs I may have to bear? Once my book is published, how do I get people to read it?

classes.title: Writing Memorable Characters
classes.description: Writing a good work of fiction begins with wrestling with the mysterious dichotomy of character: you are creating a person who is deeply a part of you—and yet is not you. If the struggle is a success, the result is a character who lives on and off the page. In this master class author Sophfronia Scott will guide an exploration of techniques for creating a powerful protagonist with a unique voice.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: How to Write a Children's Book
classes.description: Ready to turn your ideas, insights, or memories into a book for young readers? Join award-winning children's author Kate Klise as she shares her best writing tips and tricks for creating compelling works of both fiction and nonfiction. In this class, you'll learn how to create characters and conflicts that keep readers turning the pages. Come prepared to write, read, revise, and review publishing strategies in this ever-changing literary landscape.

classes.title: Unpacking Your Stories
classes.description: What if the dreaded process of "rightsizing" instead became a treasure hunt for forgotten stories and an opportunity to leave a legacy of your own values? Learn how to use storytelling to discover what you want to keep or leave behind as you move to a smaller space. You will also learn new ways to pass along your stories. If your family and friends don't want you stuff, they'll want your stories!

classes.title: Write Poetry Inspired by Visual Art
classes.description: Step into works of art to slow down, wonder, imagine, and write in new ways. Find inspiration in the fascinating shell paintings of artist Georgia O'Keeffe and in the colorful compositions of artist Alma Thomas. Discover how close looking at art can inspire diverse poetic forms and how writing can connect you more deeply to art. Experience a rich scaffolded process that deepens your looking, unveils meaningful layers in the art, and fuels your imagination. Designed for lovers of writing and art and the curious.

classes.title: From Novice to Novelist
classes.description: Deconstructs and demystifies the novel-writing process for struggling and/or aspiring writers. You'll learn how to stay organized, write in the voice of the other genders, the art of rewriting, and how to overcome your writing and marketing fears. By week's end you'll be prepared to begin work on a novel and will be equipped with the skills to perfect it. There will be time for writing and being critiqued.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Creative Writing Inspired by Visual Art
classes.description: Step into works of art to slow down, wonder, imagine, and write in new ways. Paintings by Georgia O'Keeffe, Lilla Cabot Perry, and Vanessa Bell, paired with writings by DH Lawrence, Edith Wharton, and Virginia Woolf, will inspire our creative writing. Discover how close looking at art can inspire characters and stories and how writing can connect you more deeply to art. Experience a rich scaffolded process that unveils meaningful layers in the art and fuels your imagination. Designed for lovers of writing and art and the curious.

classes.title: Reflective Writing: Give Sorrow Words
classes.description: The experience of grief is universal and yet we often feel alone and unmoored when faced with loss. In this session, discover how reflective writing can offer a creative buoy for engaging with loss. Inspired by works of visual art and poetry, participants give words to grief through a gentle series of reflective writing prompts. Experience a process in which reflection and writing become a place of comfort and a space for holding sorrow as well as remembrance. Designed for everyone.

classes.title: Reflective Writing: Winds of Change
classes.description: Discover how reflective writing offers a powerful tool for navigating change. Inspired by a masterful print of one of Japan's most innovative artists, Katsushika Hokusai, and by poetry across time, we will slow down, look closely, reflect and write to explore the metaphor of wind in our world and in our lives. Designed for all, explore how a rich series of reflective writing prompts can expand your perspectives, deepen your understandings, and open you to new ways to approach challenges and change.

classes.title: You CAN Write: Creative Writing for Anyone
classes.description: Please join in for an opportunity to write without judgment or critique! Whether you have an on-going project, have never written before, are a seasoned journal-keeper, or you simply want to play with writing, you are Welcome! Using various prompts and ideas, you will be invited to let your creativity flow in a safe space for sharing and connecting with others. No experience necessary. Only a willingness to write and hopefully share!

classes.title: The Healing Power of Words
classes.description: In challenging times, writing can strengthen us, provide comfort, and help us to grow mentally, emotionally, and spiritually. You'll learn and implement holistic, whole brain writing methods designed to provide new possibilities for healing and for telling inspiring stories. Ideal for those interested in expanding their writing and their relationship to self, others, and the world for personal expression or publication in whatever genre you prefer.

classes.title: Poetry or Memoir: Both/And Thinking About Legacy Writing
classes.description: In this class, we'll shift away from "either/or" thinking to embrace elements of poetry in memoir, and autobiographical elements in poetry. How do writers choose the form for their experiences and views? We'll read and discuss work by both canonical and contemporary writers, exploring how they present their joys and sorrows. Our responses will be oral and written, giving us the opportunity to connect to the beauty and insight of the wisest of humans: writers.

classes.title: Delicious Words: Food-Inspired Writing
classes.description: Food not only nurtures and sustains us, it's also a rich writing source. We'll explore this connection as we write of when, where, what, with whom, how, and even why we ate, using examples from the work of accomplished writers. You can apply the simple yet powerful methods you'll learn to create individual essays, stories, poems, scenes in fiction or memoir, a food blog, a family cookbook, or simply to capture special memories.

classes.title: Reflecting through Writing
classes.description: Join us for this welcoming and inclusive class that explores writing as a form of reflection. Students will investigate several topics, including relationships, nature, and identity. We will generate new writing, share writing for those who feel comfortable doing so, and give supportive and generous feedback. Each session will involve prompts to awaken your writing mind, readings of essays to inspire your own work, and time for longer generative writing. Writers at all levels of practice are welcome, as are past participants.

classes.title: Pop Goes the Poem!
classes.description: This playful, subversive workshop bursts with pop culture references, shameless product placement, and strategic profanity. Participants generate poems and prose that remix ads, memes, music, movies, and brands into sharp, witty, emotionally charged work. Through readings, discussion, and revision, writers explore voice, satire, critique, and pleasure, discovering how contemporary culture can energize language and imagery while still delivering craft, intention, and impact—encouraging bold experimentation and creative risk-taking.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Wild Writing: Jumpstart Your Storytelling
classes.description: What is it you plan to do with your one wild and precious life? - Mary Oliver We say, "I want to write," but it's hard to find time and energy. Hence, this generative workshop. From poetry to prose, micro to memoir, our class is for anyone at any stage who longs to invigorate their writing with more joy and connection. Together, we'll draft, revise, and play as we rediscover the wonder of shared creative practice.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Poetry as an Act of Attention
classes.description: In a world that often feels too loud, the simple act of paying attention becomes a radical form of care. This generative workshop invites you to slow down and allow your "serious noticing" to guide you into new patterns of thought. Drawing inspiration from across the arts including film, music, and painting, we will explore how different mediums can sharpen our internal lens. This class offers a sanctuary to experiment, observe, and generate new work that explores the possibilities of our attention.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Memoir: Writing the Experiences of Illness and Grief
classes.description: Illness and grief are formative, shattering experiences that both shape and unite us as human beings. And while both experiences can make us feel profoundly alone and isolated, the stories we read, tell, and write are powerful antidotes, offering connection and hope. In this workshop, we will apply the techniques of memoir to write about this rich landscape. In this supportive and generative workshop, we will read and write together, focusing on lessons on craft (with a focus on voice and scene) but also ensuring plenty of writing time with prompts and feedback on your work.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Characters and Voices: Write the Other
classes.description: Each poem is a step into the unknown, an opportunity to go beyond our lives and our experiences. The poem is a vessel for empathy and connection. In this generative workshop, participants will generate poems in the perspectives of others than themselves, of public and historical persona, and revise works by strengthening the voices in them. We will learn from other poets like John Berryman, Tyehimba Jess, Shara McCallumn, Natasha Trethewey, and more.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Old Land, New Eyes: The Necessity of Worldbuilding in Historical Fiction
classes.description: How do you transport readers to the past? You build the world not simply as it was, but in a manner that makes time travel feel imperative for the reader. In this flexible workshop, we will explore how to use historical context not only to create compelling characters and build richer scenes, but to select stories that matter in today's world. We will discuss the various modes of historical fiction writing, how to decide on the right language, and how to avoid anachronistic pitfalls. As we read workshop submissions, we will also read excerpts from novels and short stories and an essay or two.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Wild Words: Using Nature in Books for Kids
classes.description: This generative writing workshop will explore ways nature can shape your story world, grow your characters, and enhance your narrative in children's writing. Each class will feature writing exercises and lessons on elements of story and plot. You'll heighten your senses and get plugged into the natural world with child-like wonder. You'll leave this course with more tools, new pages, and more confidence to grow the wild story that you want to create. Nature is our constant inspiration!
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Writing the Memorable Novel: How to Deliver Emotional Impact
classes.description: This flexible workshop is intended for participants with a basic understanding of writing fundamentals. Students should already be familiar with concepts like Point of View, Theme, Plot Structure, and other core elements of storytelling, allowing the workshop to focus on deeper practice and exploration.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: If a Poem is a House: Inviting Your Reader In
classes.description: Both beginning and advanced poets sometimes struggle with making their poems accessible to a wider audience. How do we open the door of our poems to readers? Participants in this flexible workshop will receive feedback on new or older work with a focus on clarity and context while also examining recent poems that touch on these issues.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: My Life as a Child: Childhood Memoir
classes.description: Writing about your own childhood has many challenges: the limits of memory, the risk of sentimentality, and the transformation of truth over time. But it also brings great rewards: capturing the past, making meaning of experience, seeing your individual life as part of a larger historical moment. Guided by models of fine writing in this nonfiction genre, we will apply the imaginative tools of literary art to craft the raw material of our early memories in this flexible workshop.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Writing and Revising the Sensuous Poem
classes.description: Poetry becomes sensuous as opposed to sensual when a writer engages a reader's senses through attentive use of vivid and tactile imagery, a compelling auditory texture, evocative language, and thoughtful poetic architecture, thereby allowing abstract ideas to feel tangible and creating an immersive sensory experience that encourages readers to make powerful emotional connections to poems. In this flexible workshop, we will focus on ways poets draft and revise poems toward sensuousness and intimacy between readers and poets.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: All Our Voices
classes.description: Welcoming writers, fiction and nonfiction, all levels; we'll explore our individual voices, adding to the tapestry of our world. Inspired by readings, discussions of creative process, and how to engage the senses and imagination, students write from prompts, experience, and passions, sharing efforts with this flexible workshop for helpful and collegial input, deepening our voices for literary journeys ahead.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Writing Down Your Demons
classes.description: The word demon, comes from daemon, the Latin word for 'spirit,' which derives from the Greek daimon, 'divine power' or 'genius.' But how can we speak of divine power or beauty when our world rocks with loss, grief, change, and turmoil? Writing poetry allows us to see, name, and shape our demons into terrible beauty. In-class generative writing exercises, reading and discussing sample poems, plus Lynda Barry's book One! Hundred! Demons, will be our core work.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: When Your Story Refuses to Fit
classes.description: What happens when your story refuses to fit one category? This generative workshop explores how to thoughtfully combine elements from different genres while maintaining coherent voice, authentic worldbuilding, and clear stakes. Through the use of craft discussion, generative exercises, and analysis of two sample stories, we'll examine techniques for making unexpected genre combinations feel inevitable. Students will write new work and develop plans for genre blending projects.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Local Muses: The Poetry of Place
classes.description: Familiar places hold vast amounts of information, layers of echoes, memories, and presences that can deepen a poem and bring it into conversation with the living communities that surround us. In this flexible workshop, we'll explore poetic techniques for evoking place through generative prompts and examples. Participants can workshop a finished poem or something they create during the week. All are welcome, including those interested in applying what they learn to other genres, hybrid work, or lyric essays.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Rewriting History
classes.description: How can we integrate the past into fiction? In this flexible workshop, we'll think through the power of history and historical fiction as a literary form. We'll discuss how fiction can situate itself in the past without feeling didactic or stuffy. We'll also leave space to explore the importance of historical fidelity versus fabulation, and what the two different modes offer the reader.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Begin Again
classes.description: Beginning a poem does not require certainty, only attention to the world at hand. In this generative poetry workshop, we'll explore multiple entry points into poems, using place, image, and sound as guides. Prompts will invite surprise, risk, and responsiveness to contemporary landscapes and moments. Alongside generative writing, we'll discuss revision strategies and ways to recognize what a draft is asking to become.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Myths, Folktales, Family Stories, and You
classes.description: Beginning a poem does not require certainty—only attention to the world at hand. In this generative poetry workshop, we'll explore multiple entry points into poems, using place, image, and sound as guides. Prompts will invite surprise, risk, and responsiveness to contemporary landscapes and moments. Alongside generative writing, we'll discuss revision strategies and ways to recognize what a draft is asking to become.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Writing Your Imagination as Nonfiction
classes.description: Though it sounds counterintuitive, imagination is key to writing nonfiction. Making vivid the people, places, and moods you remember is what makes for the best memoir, biography, and blog writing. However, our imaginations have been muffled and discouraged. We will reinvigorate our imaginations and learn to use them effectively on the page. Our sessions will include writing, discussion of habits and practices for fostering imagination, and creative learning activities.

classes.title: Slow Flow Yoga
classes.description: This yoga class is for individuals of all levels and ages. This class teaches Hatha yoga postures, meant to release, stretch, and build body-mind-spirt awareness. Class will focus on safe alignment, building core and total-body strength, increase flexibility, and improve balance as well as concentration and breath control. Slow flow yoga is smooth, yet challenging and suitable for most abilities, including those who are new to the practice of yoga. Additionally, get the benefits of aromatherapy throughout the class. Participants should be able to get up and down from the floor. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Yoga, Creativity, and Connection Through the Chakras
classes.description: In this three-day, two-hour-per-class immersion, explore the ancient system of the chakras, sacred energetic centers, as pathways to healing, creativity, and spiritual connection. Each session weaves gentle yoga, breathwork, meditation, sound, and expressive arts to nurture emotional release and awaken intuitive flow. You'll learn to listen to your body's wisdom, translate energy into creative expression, and restore balance through movement and mindfulness. This supportive, heart-centered series offers a sacred space for integration where art, spirit, and therapeutic practice meet in harmony. Bring a yoga mat.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Fellowship Hall

classes.title: Gentle Yoga
classes.description: Learn basic yoga breathing and stretching. Yoga is a non-competitive, non-strenuous exercise which helps you relax while toning and lengthening muscles. Emphasis will be on building strength, increasing flexibility, improving balance and reducing stress. Individuals move at their own pace. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Morning Yoga Flow
classes.description: Start your day with yoga! Move through sun salutations and forward folds as you stretch, strengthen, and balance. Class will include seated and standing postures, twists, and balance poses. Modifications will be offered to support a mixed-level environment. Leave feeling strong, flexible, and centered. Previous yoga experience helpful but not required. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Gentle Yoga and Meditation
classes.description: Begin your day with mindful movement, breathwork, and meditation. This gentle yoga class starts with pranayama (yogic breathing), flows into gentle poses, and concludes with a guided exploration of various meditation techniques. You'll experience a balanced sequence of seated and standing postures, along with twists and balance work. Modifications are provided to support all levels of experience. No prior experience is required, though familiarity with yoga or meditation is always beneficial. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Gentle Yoga for Flexibility and Stability
classes.description: This class will implement breathing and gentle yoga postures to safely open and rejuvenate the body. Perfect for someone who has always wanted to try yoga as well as an experienced practitioner. We will incorporate yoga props and offer modifications to empower and help you feel great in your yoga practice! Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Enjoy the Gardens of Chautauqua through Kripalu Gentle Yoga
classes.description: Enjoy an early morning Gentle Kripalu Yoga class in a different Chautauqua garden each day. We will traverse the grounds, starting at the Discovery Garden near the Main Gate. We move to the Arboretum across Thunder Bridge, the Bishop's Garden facing the lake, and the Campbell Garden near the Miller Cottage. On Friday, we journey to the Labyrinth, ending the week with a loving kindness meditation walk and a gentle closing yoga ceremony. Afterwards, if you would like, we can bike around the loop back to our cottages, enjoying the lake, the fresh air, and the rain gardens. Bring a yoga mat.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Fellowship Hall

classes.title: Sunday Morning Gentle Yoga by the Lake
classes.description: Begin your week with meditation and a gentle Kripalu Yoga practice at the edge of the lake. Spend 90 minutes breathing, meditating and stretching while focusing on the sounds of the waves and birds. The class is designed to be a grounded contemplative Sunday morning practice (the quiet before the storm). No previous experience is necessary. Consider joining us, gathering with friends, and fostering an intimate relationship with our precious Chautauqua Lake. This class is offered on July 12, July 26, August 9 and August 23. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Yoga for Strength and Mobility
classes.description: Designed for adults who want to stay strong, mobile, and confident in daily life. We'll focus on safe, accessible yoga movements that build muscle strength, improve flexibility, and support healthy balance. Emphasis will be placed on practicing how to move safely up and down from the floor, a key skill for maintaining independence. Using exercise bands (provided by instructor), we'll add gentle resistance to enhance bone and muscle health. Bring a yoga mat and an open mind, you'll leave feeling stronger, steadier, and more at ease in your body.

classes.title: The Art of Embodied Yoga: Ease, Breath, and Heart
classes.description: Through deep breathing, slow movement, and focused attention to specific areas of the body, this workshop helps you recognize subtle signals that the body and heart are sending. As these messages register, the whole system softens, creating clarity, balance, and ease. We'll meditate, visualize, and practice basic to moderate poses with safe alignment, grounding, and heart-opening energy work to release tension and cultivate appreciation and peace. Link body with mind. All levels welcome. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Yoga for Life, Experience the Joy
classes.description: Explore the physical, emotional and spiritual benefits of yoga from a teacher with over 50 years of experience. Emphasis will be on alignment, understanding, protection and ways to incorporate yoga into your life with joy and confidence. All levels welcome. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Yoga for Flexibility
classes.description: Slow flow yoga builds flexibility, strength, and inner calm. All bodies and levels welcome. Gentle to medium. Modifications are offered. We do breathing, stretches, and poses that align and strengthen the body, ending with relaxation to integrate. Mindful movement nurtures awareness of energy flow in the body and connection with the world. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Vinyasa Flow Yoga
classes.description: Vinyasa Flow Yoga allows you to fluidly move from one pose to the next while connecting their breathing to their movements. The class starts with a short breathing exercise followed by thoughtful sequences with variations to modify, intensify or challenge the body by altering the pace or duration of poses and the frequency that they are repeated, and ends with gentle movements carrying you to a relaxing position. You will leave the class physically, mentally and spiritually refreshed in a light and strong body with a calm mind. Some yoga experience is required. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Mindful Flow Yoga
classes.description: Join us for vinyasa flow classes to help you reconnect body, breath, and mind. The classes include an emphasis on breath and body awareness, so you can fine tune your practice to meet you where you are. We will work on building strength as well as awareness of the energy body. Some yoga experience is recommended, and variations will be offered for those with a strong practice. You will leave feeling energized, restored and grounded. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Yoga with a Flair
classes.description: This class welcomes all ages and levels of ability. We will focus on the mind, body and spirit while toning the body, gaining flexibility and learning a variety of breathing, balancing and meditation techniques. You will leave the class relaxed and energized with a sense of appreciation for your body and its capabilities while having fun. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Tai Chi for Health
classes.description: You will learn a simple form of Tai Chi that is designed to improve your health, flexibility and balance. As you practice each part of the form, your confidence and ability to continue doing the form after the class ends will increase. You are taught the movements in a safe and easy manner following a stepwise progressive method that was developed by Dr. Paul Lam of the Tai Chi for Health Institute.

classes.title: Tai Chi for Balance and Bone Health
classes.description: Tai Chi for Balance and Bone Health combines Sun and Yang styles to produce slow graceful movements. It will improve your health and wellness, internal energy, and the ability to manage stress. This course also provides participants with an introduction to the essential principles and styles of Tai Chi. The course is suitable for all abilities. Please wear comfortable, loose clothing and laced shoes.

classes.title: Intro to Tai Chi and Qigong for Wellness
classes.description: These two forms of Asian movement meditation offer many roads to good health. Research at Harvard University, as well as elsewhere, demonstrated that improvements in balance, blood pressure and flexibility, among other benefits, can be expected with regular practice. These systems of movement, meditation and breathing bring you to a calm centered self, more capable of being fully in the moment. For people of all abilities and requires no previous experience. Please wear comfortable clothing and cotton socks.

classes.title: Tai Chi for Joint Health
classes.description: Tai Chi for a Joint Health offers many benefits for good health. Research studies show that improvements in balance, lower blood pressure and cholesterol, and greater flexibility can be expected with regular practice. You will learn an entire Tai Chi set with continuous graceful movements. This course also gives participants an introduction to the essential principles and styles of Tai Chi. The course is suitable for all abilities. Please wear comfortable, loose clothing and laced shoes.

classes.title: Barre Fitness Class
classes.description: A full body workout! Change your body: tone, sculpt, burn fat and build a lean physique. Barre classes combine dance, Pilates and yoga fused with cardio and fitness elements for the most effective results. The classes are set to music and utilize the ballet barre (or chair). A fun, high energy and challenging class that will bring you results. Bring a yoga mat.

classes.title: Morning Stretch Class
classes.description: Begin your day with a morning stretch! Improve your flexibility and mobility. Help your muscles work more efficiently and effectively to improve posture, increase muscle blood flow, decrease muscle soreness and back pain, help prevent injuries, reduce stress and improve your ability to perform daily activities. In this class we will explore all joint ranges of motion and stretch our muscles from head to toe. Join us to feel better for a healthier you!

classes.title: Pilates Mat Class
classes.description: Enhance your body and mind! This class is an excellent total body workout that improves one's core strength, spinal stability, flexibility, mobility, control, coordination, balance, breath, posture and body awareness. The mat work is the essence and foundation of the Pilates method of body conditioning. Students will learn and perform the specialized floor Pilates exercises on a mat. Please join us to rejuvenate your body and enhance your overall well-being!

classes.title: Basic Self-Defense Seminar
classes.description: This one-hour seminar will cover basic self-defense based on Shotokan karate. Students will learn both offensive and defensive moves to protect themselves. No prior experience needed.

classes.title: Shotokan Karate and Self-Defense Basics
classes.description: This course will be two 1.5-hour sessions of self-defense and Shotokan karate. Students will be taught proper stances, punches and kicks. Basic defenses against punches, kicks, grabs, and weapons will be covered, as well as the white belt kata if time allows. Please wear comfortable clothing that you can move in, such as work out cotton pants, yoga leggings, and t-shirts as well as non-slip shoes.

classes.title: Rush Hour Mid-Morning Crunch
classes.description: Join me for your full body and functional workout. We will focus on strength, mobility and core movements. We will use a variety of equipment including but not limited to the use of dumbbells, kettlebells, balls and bodyweight exercises. Workouts will consist of Tabata, HIIT, and Moving Circuits. I look forward to being apart of your fitness journey again this season.

classes.title: Forest Bathing at Chautauqua
classes.description: Experience the healing benefits of nature! Forest Bathing, also known as Forest Therapy, is a slow, mindful immersion in nature that originated in Japan. During a single morning session, the guide will lead you in voluntary activities called invitations as we slowly move through the forest and connect with the environment using all of our senses. This practice helps participants let go of the busyness of everyday life and experience the soothing sensuality of nature. Forest Bathing is deeply grounding, has many health benefits, including lowering blood pressure and boosting the immune system.

classes.title: The Alexander Technique: Movement with Grace
classes.description: Sit up straight! yelled your mother. But when you did, it felt tight, pushy and uncomfortable. You can be poised and comfortable without effort. The Alexander Technique uses sensing, anatomy and teacher's light touch for graceful, flexible, fluid and expressive movements. Everyone can open joints, free tight muscles, reduce pain and change habits. Your mother would be proud.

classes.title: Introduction to Ayurveda
classes.description: Discover the ancient Indian system of holistic healing in this beginner friendly course. Explore Ayurveda's core principles-doshas, digestion, daily routines, and natural balance-while learning simple practices to support well-being. You'll gain practical tools for nourishing the body, mind, and spirit. Ideal for anyone seeking a grounded and bio-individual approach to wellness. Monday and Tuesday sessions will be held in Turner Conference Room. Wednesday session will be held in the Turner 205, the culinary classroom to create some Ayurvedic recipes.

classes.title: All Abilities Strength Training for Low Back Health
classes.description: This class focuses on gaining strength for the whole body, with an emphasis on ensuring low back health. The course follows the strength exercises and low back rehab protocols Professor Stuart McGill, Professor Emeritus of Spine Biomechanics from the University of Waterloo, in Waterloo, Ontario Canada. Emphasis is on learning spine sparing techniques to build a strong core, learning proper squatting techniques for lower body strength and how to perform compound movements for total body strength.

classes.title: Nordic Pole Walking for Cardio, Strength, and Better Balance
classes.description: Nordic Pole Walking is the perfect total body exercise. It not only provides a cardio-respiratory workout for the heart and lungs, but in my class I will teach you how to use the poles to perform an upper body strength workout, a lower body strength workout and balance/stability exercises too. It's a "4 in 1" workout that is great for beginners and challenging for fitness enthusiasts who want to learn a new fitness routine.

classes.title: The Alexander Technique: Mapping Activities
classes.description: Aching muscles? Sore joints? Are your everyday activities painful? We'll find the joints and muscles you need to use and be sure you're engaging them correctly. By discovering the anatomy behind the movement and sensing yourself fully, the teacher's light touch will help you move more easily. Whether you're sitting at the computer, walking, dancing, playing piano, or tennis, let's get the aches and pains out, bring in ease and freedom.

classes.title: Nature Immersion, Forest Bathing
classes.description: Immerse yourself in nature through stillness, movement, your senses, and kind intention. Join us outside to learn five meditation and embodiment practices that help you reconnect with nature, relieve anxiety, improve health, and deeply appreciate the environment and the present moment. Join Dr. Annie Weisbrod, environmental scientist, Buddhist teacher and author of one of the largest meditation studies published for this special experiential session.

classes.title: The Alexander Technique: 5 Classic Studies
classes.description: How should I be moving? Each day you will learn a different classic movement/position of Alexander: standing, sitting, bending over, standing up from a chair, and walking, with balance, alignment, and poise. Bring your own activities which use those movements to discover new ways to be comfortable. Teacher's light touch will help you sense more, ease muscles and move freely. Next Amp lecture = comfortable sitting!

classes.title: Self-Defense and Aiki/Karate Skills
classes.description: This class is a basic introduction to the martial arts. I will provide you with some easy to apply self-defense techniques along with exercises to improve your mind, body, and spirit. If you are interested in the history of the martial arts there will be something for you. We will look at both the physical and metaphysical side of self-defense.

classes.title: Breath and Health Longevity: Unlocking the Power Within
classes.description: In our fast-paced world, how we breathe is often overlooked, yet it holds incredible power over our physical and mental well-being. This is a transformative journey into understanding how your breath influences everything from stress responses and belly fat to digestive, brain, and recovery health. By understanding the profound effects of your breath, you can take control of your physical and mental well-being without the need for elaborate routines or equipment. Learn and participate in diaphragmatic breath exercises, "core" recovery exercises, and breath patterns to create health longevity!

classes.title: A World of Wellness
classes.description: From the annual World Happiness Report to body odors and foods to dental health, this class offers a potpourri of wellness findings from research and experts that may surprise, affirm, and motivate participants. Just why has Finland ranked #1 in global happiness for eight consecutive years? What does garlic do to body sweat? Which sports have been linked to a longer lifespan? An array of ideas from different areas of wellness will be offered.

classes.title: Sound Immersion Meditation
classes.description: Prepare for a deep experience of rest while being serenaded by cascading sounds of crystal singing bowls, Asian gongs, tinkling chimes, gentle ocean waves, and much more, to soothe, calm, and settle the body, mind, and spirit. Jane's background of many years in the study and practice of Ancient Healing Arts, and Charles' lifelong involvement in professional musical endeavors, combine for a fully immersive soundscape experience. Chairs will be available or bring a yoga mat if comfortable sitting on the floor. Some yoga mats will be available to use.

classes.title: Meditation for Grounding and Prescencing
classes.description: This series will use breathing and body-based awareness to calm the nervous system and orient to the present. Each session will begin with short instruction followed by a guided meditation. Techniques shared in these sessions are informed by Vipassana meditation, yogic approaches, and somatic approaches. Science-based practices to cue the nervous system for calm will also be shared. This series is open to individuals wishing to try meditation for the first time as well as experienced individuals wishing to practice in a group. Meghan Collins is Certified Meditation Teacher.

classes.title: Longevity Science
classes.description: Live better, longer. Make better daily health-care decisions based upon the best peer reviewed research. Learn how fitness, rich social life, Mediterranean diet and more has been shown to increase lifespan by years. Longevity research shows combining healthy habits increases life expectancy by more than a decade. How to use AI for superb medical education.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: 7 Days a Week, 1 Day and 1 Bite at a Time
classes.description: Holistic aging in good health means caring for your physical, mental, and emotional well-being through balanced nutrition, regular exercise, mindfulness, and strong social connections. Every week, 1 Day at a Time, making thoughtful choices—such as selecting, preparing and sharing nutrient dense foods, staying active physically and mentally, integrates healthy practices into the fabric of daily life. These small habits, consistently practiced, support long-term health, vitality, and longevity, positively influencing not only your own well-being but also that of the close circles around you. Wednesday class is in Turner 104. Friday class is in Turner 205, the culinary classroom. Bring a yoga mat if possible and a notebook.

classes.title: Cancer Screening: More Harm Than Good?
classes.description: Cancer screening searches for hidden disease, to "catch it early". Is this always beneficial? Detecting cancer early can also lead to overdiagnosis and overtreatment, resulting in significant physical and emotional harm. We will discuss the fundamentals of cancer screening and explore the perils inherent in this trade-off. The class will largely be interactive.

classes.title: Sugar Smart: A Two-Part Journey to Better Health
classes.description: Join us for a five-day journey toward better health and balanced living. In Part 1 (Monday–Wednesday), discover how simple changes in eating order, timing, and daily movement can improve blood sugar and energy. In Part 2 (Thursday–Friday) with Chef Linda Ruberto, we'll cook together, plan meals, and enjoy healthy tastings. This hands-on workshop blends knowledge, practice, and community; making it easier, and more enjoyable, to stay on track for lasting well-being.

classes.title: Playful Posture Practice: Preventing Forward Head Posture
classes.description: Modern habits like phone use, computer work, and daily tasks often lead to tight muscles and poor posture. This gentle yoga class helps counter those effects with movements that improve alignment, flexibility, and strength. Through lighthearted, mindful practice, you'll learn simple techniques to reduce forward-head posture and move through your day with greater ease and comfort.

classes.title: Adult Beginner and Intermediate Sailing
classes.description: This course is for adult sailors of all experience levels. It includes on-the-water, classroom, and dockside instruction. Each day features a brief lecture, sailing games, and at least two hours on the water. Students learn sailing terminology, boat safety, sail trim, wind and weather identification, knots, capsize recovery, safe handling, and rigging/derigging of a Sunfish dinghy. Intermediate students can deepen their skills with instructor help. Perfect for fun adventures on Chautauqua Lake and learning a lifelong skill.

classes.title: Advanced Sailing
classes.description: This course is for advanced sailors of all ages who want to learn competitive sailing. It covers advanced terminology, racing strategies, race starts, spinnaker use, roll tacking, right of way, sportsmanship, teamwork, and rigging/derigging of Lasers and 420s. Students are assigned boats based on skill, physical ability, and goals. Participants must sail independently on all points of sail and perform basic tacking and jibing maneuvers. Perfect for those who want to elevate their sailing skills. John R. Turney Sailing Center staff is trained annually and led by US Sailing Level 1-certified instructors.

classes.title: Optimist Beginner Youth Sailing
classes.description: This course will teach the basics of rigging a boat, basic boat handling, sailing fundamentals, knots, weather, sportsmanship and water safety. The Optimist (or Opti) is the biggest dinghy class in the world with over 150,000 kids sailing in over 100 countries. It is a stable, forgiving platform designed for kids to learn how to sail and enjoy time on the water. John R. Turney Sailing Center staff is trained annually and led by US Sailing Level 1-certified instructors.

classes.title: Teen Beginner and Intermediate Sailing
classes.description: This course is for teen sailors of all experience levels. It includes on-the-water, classroom, and dockside instruction. Each day features a brief lecture, sailing games, and at least two hours on the water. Students learn sailing terminology, boat safety, sail trim, wind and weather identification, knots, capsize recovery, safe handling, and rigging/derigging of a Sunfish dinghy. Intermediate students can deepen their skills with instructor help. Perfect for fun adventures on Chautauqua Lake and learning a lifelong skill. John R. Turney Sailing Center staff is trained annually and led by US Sailing Level 1-certified instructors.

classes.title: Dungeons and Dragons for Beginners
classes.description: All ages welcome! Interested in experiencing or trying out collaborative storytelling role-playing games (RPGs) like Dungeons and Dragons, but don't know how to jump in? Learn about the history and culture of RPGs and experience your first adventure from character creation to battling dragons. No experience necessary.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Fellowship Hall

classes.title: Standup Paddleboard (SUP) Guided Gentle Stretch Class
classes.description: The Sports Club is offering Standup Paddleboard (SUP) Guided Gentle Stretch Class. SUP rental included.

classes.title: Standup Paddleboard (SUP) Beginner Class
classes.description: The Sports Club is offering Standup Paddleboard (SUP) lessons for beginners. Enjoy on-shore instruction followed by time in the water. SUP rental included.

classes.title: Fun Activities with Pets
classes.description: Pets can impact the health of the families with whom they live. Participating in enjoyable activities is rewarding for you, your family, your friends, and your pet. Make family play-time with your pet a happy habit. Maintaining sustainable, realistic, positive changes in your schedule supports solution-focused confidence building and a realistic routine of physical activity to share with your pet. Pets are strong, positive motivators for healthy, regular physical activity.

classes.title: Beginner Pickleball
classes.description: Pickleball is a multi-generation paddle sport that is exploding worldwide. It is easier to learn with much less court to cover than tennis. Adults with orthopedic and other health issues can still remain active with pickleball, played on a court the same size as a doubles badminton court. We will cover strategy, scoring, the serve, basic shots (block and punch volley, lob, forehand and backhand) as well as more advanced shots (spin, dink and drop). Learn how to play the No Volley Zone (kitchen), where to position yourself on the court and how to safely handle shots hit behind you. Must wear court shoes for this class. Court shoes are athletic style footwear with a smooth sole which allows for friction free movement across the court surface.

classes.title: Introduction to Geocaching
classes.description: If you've ever wanted to wander haplessly, all while having your sanity judged by others, then this is the course for you! We will dive into all things geocaching. Considered a real-world, outdoor treasure-hunting game, you will learn everything from how to read a map (OG caching) vs. modern smartphone hunting, hiding/finding techniques, container types/puzzle boxes, and how you can contribute to this global activity in your own town. The course will be conducted both within a classroom setting and around the grounds of Chautauqua.

classes.title: Mah Jongg for Beginners
classes.description: It's MAH JONGG! The game that has been enjoyed in the USA for nearly a century has soared in popularity in recent years. Don't be left behind. Get on board the Mah Jongg Train. Learn in a low-stress, friendly environment with an experienced instructor. You will learn how to read the National Mah Jongg League card, distribution of tiles, the Charleston and choose sections for possible winning hands. National Mah Jongg League card included.

classes.title: Introduction to Kayaking
classes.description: Kayaking has become a popular outdoor activity for all ages and ability levels. Now you can learn the basics of kayaking right here on Chautauqua Lake. This class will cover the fundamentals of kayaking, including safety practices, kayak design, launching and landing, paddling techniques, and steering maneuvers.

classes.title: Bridge for Absolute Beginners
classes.description: You may not know a trump from a finesse, but you'll be playing and defending real bridge hands by the end of the week! Come to learn for the first time or to learn "MiniBridge", the new teaching technique for fast-start play. Be the kind of partner bridge players ask for again. Come to play. Partner optional but not necessary.

classes.title: Mah Jongg One-Session Rules Refresher
classes.description: You know how to play Mah Jongg but sometimes feel rusty on rules. The walls, deal, play … in which direction does each go? How do Charleston passes proceed? When can you blind pass? What are modifications for three players? Two players? How do you trade or use a joker? When can you NOT call a tile? What makes a hand "dead?" What common courtesies are practiced? If you already know how to play, this one-session rules refresher is for you. If you have never played and want to learn, take Mah Jongg for Beginners.

classes.title: Hiking Hounds
classes.description: Grab a leash and hit the Chautauqua Trail! Hiking is a great way to exercise, relieve stress and strengthen the bond between you and your canine companion. Being in nature is refreshing and provides rich sensory stimulation for your dog. Enjoy the outdoors as we hike approximately 1.5 miles on wooded paths.
classes.location: Golf Learning Center CHQ Trail Entrance Meeting Point

classes.title: Card Games of the World
classes.description: An opportunity to learn popular card games from other countries! Each day, we will learn a new card game, review the game from the day before, and end by playing the game of the day with each other. The final day will be spent playing one or all of our new games together. All experience levels are welcome.

classes.title: How to Defend a Bridge Hand
classes.description: Your bridge game is not complete if you only play Declarer! Fully half the time you'll be on defense. Do you know what to do? Learn the leads, the signals, the attack and the counting which will please your partner and demoralize your opponents. Basic defense should be in everyone's repertoire. Leave bidding behind for a week and let's play!

classes.title: First Aid: What Your Veterinarian Would Like You to Know
classes.description: With 25 years as an emergency veterinarian and even longer as a pet parent, I love helping others learn how to provide the best preventative and emergency care for their animals. Using a Red Cross First Aid text as our guide, we will discuss what to include in first aid kits for home and car, how to navigate urgent and emergency situations, and how to make decisions alongside your veterinary team. We will explore questions such as: What truly counts as an emergency? How do we decide which tests or treatments are necessary and which are elective? The class will include teaching time, open discussion, and plenty of Q and A.

classes.title: Responsible Pet Ownership
classes.description: Journey through the essentials of responsible pet ownership while learning about basic veterinary care and why it matters. Participants will gain insight into pet body language and behavior, explore the foundations of positive reinforcement training, and discover creative enrichment activities. Learn how enrichment strengthens the bond between pets and their people while supporting physical, mental, and emotional well-being.

classes.title: Tabletop Games Preview
classes.description: Get a taste of the week's offerings with Tabletop Games: Dungeons & Dragons and Beyond! This one-time event will give participants an early look at the week-long course being offered on tabletop games with your GM for the week, Colin Epstein. Options on tap include the classic Dungeons & Dragons, as well as the independent games that we'll be playing during the week-long course.

classes.title: Tabletop Games Dungeons & Dragons and Beyond
classes.description: Collaborative storytelling at its finest; experience the magic of tabletop games with professional game-runner, Colin Epstein! Colin has introduced the joy of Dungeons & Dragons and other games to players of all ages and now brings it to the Chautauqua community. Each day will feature a different game, and a new adventure for players to pursue. We'll cover the classic D&D, of course, in addition to independent games from other publishers highlighting different approaches to the collaborative storytelling at the heart of all role-playing games. Players of all experience levels welcomed! This single day course is being offered Monday - Friday. This is the registration for the Monday session.

classes.title: Intermediate Bid and Play Bridge
classes.description: Play pre-dealt lesson hands illustrating principles of declarer bidding and play, defensive bidding and play. Players should have one or more years of playing experience plus a firm understanding of the standard American bidding style. We will explore recent bidding innovations without judgement.

classes.title: Celebrating Connections with Pets
classes.description: Pets can impact the health of the families with whom they live. Participating in enjoyable activities is rewarding for you, your family, your friends, and your pet. Make family playtime with your pet a happy habit. Maintaining sustainable, realistic, positive changes in your schedule supports solution-focused confidence building and a realistic routine of physical activity to share with your pet. Pets are strong, positive motivators for healthy, regular physical activity.

classes.title: Storytelling and The Sports Documentary
classes.description: This course explores the power of storytelling through the lens of the Sports Documentary. Attendees will learn the basic building blocks of a documentary, how to identify a strong subject, and how to develop a critical eye as a viewer. Short-form documentaries will be screened and discussed and true stories of the life-changing power of storytelling will be examined.

classes.title: Trick Dogs Walk Nicely on Leash
classes.description: Monday: Intro to reward-based dog training. Tuesday: Loose-leash walking. Wednesday: Canine massage. Thursday: Tricks. Friday: Trick-off! Other topics may be covered as well such as Ask-The-Trainer, leash reactivity. Friday will be an optional competition with fabulous prizes.

classes.title: Mah Jongg Strategy
classes.description: You know the basics, now it's time to level up your game! This dynamic Mah Jongg strategy class is designed for players who understand the fundamentals of the game and wish to improve their strategy. We'll dive into the secrets of smart tile management, mastering the Charleston, choosing a winning section and line, reading your opponents, and defensive play. Expect lively discussion, friendly competition, and plenty of "aha" moments that will leave you calling "Mah Jongg!"

classes.title: Animal Welfare
classes.description: Explore the world of pets through an engaging look at animal sheltering, veterinary care, training, and pet-related laws. Participants will learn what it takes to keep animals healthy, safe, and well cared for, while gaining insight into responsible pet ownership and community roles that support animals and the people who love them.

classes.title: Learn to Play Canasta
classes.description: Join a fun and engaging class to learn the classic card game, Canasta for two, three, or four players. Learn basics of the game such as forming melds and building canastas. Understand how to count points and apply bonuses and penalties. Learn strategies, such as: how to manage cards effectively and the risks and rewards of freezing the discard pile. Suitable for beginners as well as those who may have forgotten some rules. Includes instruction, demonstration, and practice.

classes.title: Darts for Self-Development or Competition
classes.description: Darts range somewhere between a competitive sport and a charming leisure activity. Darts have an interesting history. The activity is accessible to all skill levels and is easy to learn. It is not restricted by age, gender, mobility, venue, climate, and other conditions, and is suitable for a wide range of occasions. It can be played at home with family, at a local pub, or even league play. Playing darts is very beneficial both physically and psychologically.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Fellowship Hall

classes.title: Vibrant Vegetables
classes.description: There's no need to disguise vegetables or smother them with heavy sauces, let them shine! Learn simple cooking techniques, complementary flavors, and a selection of recipes for side dishes that feature seasonal produce. Even the pickiest eater might be inspired to take a bite! Please note that recipes in this class may not be vegetarian or vegan.

classes.title: Sexy Little Tart Class: Gluten Free Tarts with Om Nohm Bakery
classes.description: Come make fancy little tarts with local fruit, gluten free oat crusts and a variety of delicious, rich fillings, creams and toppings. Early local summer fruits include strawberries, blueberries and cherries. Vegan options. (Nuts present.) Eat your tarts or take them home!

classes.title: Farmers' Market Meals
classes.description: Meals made with fresh, local products are one of the best things about summer in Western New York. In this class, Chautauqua Institution's Bestor Fresh Market finds will inspire flavorful, easy-to-prepare dinners that highlight ingredients at their peak and make seasonal selections shine.

classes.title: Single Skillet Sensations
classes.description: Influenced by the layout of Chautauqua Institution's learning kitchen and by busy schedules seeking simple suppers, this class will feature approachable dishes that can be prepared on your stovetop using just one skillet, maybe a bowl or two, and a short list of ingredients.

classes.title: Pizza Party with Om Nohm Bakery
classes.description: Come make gluten free pizza with us; we'll start with hearty homemade Om Nohm Pizza crust and sauces, featuring local produce and savory fillings. Vegan options. (Nut free class.)

classes.title: Scones with Om Nohm Bakery
classes.description: Join us for hands-on scone baking with Om Nohm Gluten Free Bakery, featuring local produce. We'll bake and eat both sweet and savory scones, with a variety of toppings, vegan options available. (Nut free class.)

classes.title: Seafood Made Simple
classes.description: Preparing seafood can be intimidating for even a trained chef, but with quality ingredients and uncomplicated techniques, the ocean can inspire quick and delicious meals perfect for a busy weeknight. We'll learn tried and true ways to prepare a variety of proteins that take the "scary" out of the sea!

classes.title: Tastes Like Chicken
classes.description: Chicken is reasonable choice when it comes to affordable, healthy meals but why is it so boring? It doesn't have to be! Learn three easy recipes for preparing flavorful chicken dishes that will please your palate and your budget and make chicken anything but ordinary.

classes.title: Homemade Quiche with Om Nohm Bakery
classes.description: Join us to make the most delicious homemade Om Nohm quiches, a CHQ regional favorite for 9 years, featuring local produce, local organic eggs, savory cream cheese butter crust and good humor. All gluten free and vegetarian ingredients. Recipe easily translates to non-gf kitchens too. (Nut free class.) Everyone goes home with quiche!

classes.title: Summer Meal Salads with Om Nohm Bakery
classes.description: Let's play with local ingredients; learn Om Nohm's Food Truck Favorites, and you will go home with a pile of summery hearty meal salads! All ingredients are gluten free and vegetarian with vegan optional. (Nuts present.)

classes.title: Will Good Cooking: Make Cornbread, Not War
classes.description: Step into an interactive, down-home cooking experience where Southern comfort meets leftover love. In each class, you'll cook right alongside me, learning hands-on techniques, tasting as you go, and taking home full recipes so you can recreate every bite. "Make Cornbread, Not War", learn the art of making and cooking with cornbread featuring Mississippi eggs benedict, a Southern take on breakfast icon.

classes.title: Will Good Cooking: Reboot Your Food
classes.description: Step into an interactive, down-home cooking experience where Southern comfort meets leftover love. In each class, you'll cook right alongside me, learning hands-on techniques, tasting as you go, and taking home full recipes so you can recreate every bite. Reboot Your Food, turn leftovers and pantry partials into a decadent dessert featuring Bread Pudding, a sweet treat concocted by resourceful Southerners.

classes.title: Will Good Cooking: The Holy Trinity and the Pope
classes.description: Step into an interactive, down-home cooking experience where Southern comfort meets leftover love. In each class, you'll cook right alongside me, learning hands-on techniques, tasting as you go, and taking home full recipes so you can recreate every bite. "The Holy Trinity and the Pope", build Cajun flavor with onions, bell peppers, and celery featuring Maque Choux, a fresh vegetable mash-up of Native American and Cajun cuisine.

classes.title: Bienvenue to a Traditional French Onion Tarte Feast
classes.description: Discover essentials of a perfect French dejeuner in this French-inspired hands-on session. This classic French Onion Tarte combines onions, flaky pastry crust, cream, eggs and cheese. Using accessible ingredients, transform basic onions into a culinary favorite. No French meal is complete without greens tossed with French vinaigrette and a warm crusty baguette. To finish, create a delicious dessert. A truly distinctive French experience. Bon Appetit! Recipes, fact sheets, and aprons provided.

classes.title: Bienvenue to a Traditional French Salmon in Puff Pastry Feast
classes.description: Discover essentials of a perfect French meal in this French-inspired hands-on session. Classic Salmon in Puff Pastry combines salmon fillets, scallions, mustard and honey wrapped in puff pastry as main course. Using accessible ingredients, transform this dish into an upscale culinary favorite. Fresh asparagus with champagne vinaigrette will accompany the meal and to finish, create a show-stopper dessert. A truly distinctive French experience! Bon Appetit! Recipes, fact sheets, and aprons provided.
