classes.title: Growing and Cooking with Edible Flowers and Herbs
classes.description: Learn how to plant, maintain, and use edible flowers and herbs. We will discuss the many culinary uses for both edible flowers and herbs and create some sweet and savory items to sample in the classroom. You will also discover many unique and beautiful ways to decorate your culinary delights using edible flowers and herbs.

classes.title: The Judgment of Paris Wine Tasting
classes.description: While we cannot exactly recreate the original "Judgment of Paris", a landmark blind tasting competition held on May 24, 1976, where a panel of French wine experts blindly compared top-quality French wines against California wines. To everyone's astonishment, California wines triumphed in both the red and white wine categories, securing first place in both categories. In this class, we will taste and compare California and French Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvignon (or a Cabernet blend). Each of the six wine selections consists of an approximately 2-ounce pour.

classes.title: Understanding Sparkling Wine
classes.description: We will cover six sparkling wines from Champagne, greater France, England, Spain, Italy, and the United States. Over the one-hour course of tasting and education, you will broaden your understanding of sparkling wine production, its effect on the product and understand key styles from each given region. Each of the six wine selections consists of an approximately 2-ounce pour.

classes.title: Bourbon: The Spirit of America
classes.instructor: Frank T. Becker & Laura Secrist Becker
classes.description: Bourbon whiskey is indeed our American spirit! In this two-hour class, you will explore the enchanting flavors of this amber beverage. We'll learn about what bourbon really is, how bourbon is made, how it differs from other whiskeys such as Scotch. We'll touch on some of its history. Of course, you will learn how to enjoy bourbon. Included is an opportunity to taste a select array of fine bourbons to make the course a truly spirited experience!

classes.title: Sipping Through the History of American Whiskey
classes.instructor: Frank T. Becker & Laura Secrist Becker
classes.description: Whiskey history is American history, from the Whiskey Rebellion to the present. In this two-hour class we'll delve into the tumultuous history of America's spirit while sampling whiskeys that present a tribute to its history. We'll sip our way through America's attack on its citizens in the Whiskey Rebellion, then its failed attempt to control morality with Prohibition, and on to the recent Craft Distillery Boom. History was never more fun, or tasty!

classes.title: Whiskey Tour of the World
classes.instructor: Frank T. Becker & Laura Secrist Becker
classes.description: Whiskey (or "whisky" in Scottish parlance), the complex amber spirit distilled from grain in Scotland, Ireland, Japan, Canada and the United States. This two-hour course will be an interactive (and tasty!) way to learn how whiskey is made, and the differences among the various types. A little history, including the effect of prohibition in the USA, will also be discussed. Of course, no discussion of whiskeys is complete without a wee dram, so the course will include a tasting of selected examples of fine whiskeys from around the world.

classes.title: Benchmark Wine Tasting
classes.description: Ever wonder if that wine is truly worth $100 or more? Here is a rare opportunity to try six benchmark wines, all $100 or more, that hail from the most celebrated wine regions. The tasting will consist of one Champagne, White Burgundy, Red Burgundy, Red Bordeaux, Brunello di Montalcino, Napa Cabernet. Each of the six wine selections consists of an approximately 2-ounce pour.

classes.title: Masters Series Culinary Masterclass: Chef Nyesha Arrington
classes.description: See culinary mastery up close as acclaimed chef, restaurateur, and television personality Nyesha Arrington — one of the most influential voices in food today — presents an exclusive Masters Series experience that blends refined techniques, creative storytelling, and soulful flavor. Designed for curious cooks and serious food lovers alike, this intimate Masters Series program offers live demonstration, real-time Q&A, and rare insight into the techniques, mindset, and creative process of a chef shaping modern cuisine. The unforgettable experience kicks off Arrington's multiday Chautauqua residency during Week Eight, "The Future of Food: Climate, Technology and the Next Agricultural Revolution." For a greater look into the role of food in telling our personal and collective stories, Arrington joins the Chautauqua Lecture Series on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. Later that evening, she hosts an exclusive Guest Chef's Dinner, providing patrons an elevated dining experience at the historic Athenaeum Hotel.

classes.title: Masters Series Culinary Masterclass: Chef Darian Bryan
classes.description: Bold flavor, big personality, and unforgettable food take center stage in this dynamic Masters Series class with Chef Darian Bryan, one of Western New York's most celebrated culinary voices. Known for merging fine dining techniques with the vibrant soul of Caribbean cuisine, Chef Darian delivers an experience that is as entertaining as it is inspiring.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: Good Food Belongs to People, Not a Landfill
classes.description: At the intersection of food insecurity and climate change lies one powerful opportunity: food rescue. Food waste and food insecurity are often treated as separate crises — yet they stem from the same structural inefficiencies in our food system. In the United States, up to 40% of food produced goes uneaten, even as 1 in 7 households face food insecurity. Most wasted food ends up in landfills, where it becomes a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions. 412 Food Rescue in Pittsburgh is transforming how communities respond to these challenges. By mobilizing volunteers through innovative, people-powered technology, the organization rescues fresh, nutritious food that would otherwise go to waste and delivers it directly to neighbors experiencing food insecurity. In this way, the organization operates at the intersection of food waste and environmental sustainability, redirecting surplus food to communities experiencing food insecurity while reducing landfill methane emissions. In this session, leadership from 412 Food Rescue will examine how technology-enabled logistics, volunteer mobilization, and cross-sector partnerships can serve as civic infrastructure — addressing hunger, advancing environmental sustainability, and strengthening local food systems. Participants will explore how surplus food recovery functions not as charity, but as systems-level intervention in both public health and climate resilience that has national and global impact.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: From Spirit to Shelf — Inside Mezcal & Whiskey Manufacturing in Mexico
classes.description: Go beyond the glass and into the heart of artisanal spirits production in this immersive Masters Series class presented by Laika Spirits. This special program brings two master distillers—one of mezcal and one of whiskey—directly from Mexico to Chautauqua for an insider look at how some of today's most compelling spirits are made, transported, and shared with the world. Joined by close colleague and brand importer Ismael Gomez, distillers Txomin and Carlos will share vivid images and firsthand stories from the regions where their spirits are produced, offering rare insight into traditional techniques, regional terroir, and the cultural heritage behind each bottle. Together, they will explore the realities of modern spirits production, including the challenges and opportunities of importing handcrafted products into the American market. Designed as a conversational and engaging experience, the class blends storytelling, visual presentation, and open dialogue. Guests will have the opportunity to ask questions, deepen their understanding of mezcal and whiskey production, and gain a clearer picture of the journey from raw ingredient to finished spirit. Perfect for curious drinkers, spirits enthusiasts, and anyone interested in craftsmanship, culture, and global trade, this Masters Series class offers a rare behind-the-scenes look at the people and processes shaping today's premium spirits landscape.

classes.title: Who Does it Better?
classes.description: In this fun class we will try three Sauvignon Blanc and three Cabernet Sauvignon, each being from a different region or country. Terroir (a French wine term that means how the wine expresses the climate, soil, and people), will be at the center of our discussion as you try and compare the wines. Each of the six wine selections consists of an approximately 2-ounce pour.

classes.title: Is it worth it? Chardonnay and Pinot Noir Edition
classes.description: This is one of Sam Whitmore's favorite classes to teach. Most people have a preconceived idea that higher price equals higher quality, that is not always the case. This blind tasting class will challenge your palate to try and decipher which wine costs more ranging from $15 up to $80. The wines will include three each of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. After tasting through all the wines we will reveal the wines and prices. It is harder than you think!

classes.title: Understanding Napa Cabernet Sauvignon
classes.description: Taste your way through six unique sub-AVA's (American Viticultural Area) in Napa Valley to better understand the unique micro-climates and soil compositions impact on the final wine. We will try a selection of high-quality Napa Cabernet Sauvignons. Each of the six wine selections consists of an approximately 2-ounce pour.

classes.title: Chocolate Since 1776 with Samples: Monday Session
classes.description: No matter one's political beliefs, most people love chocolate! This chocolate talk with substantial samples is the perfect course for the "America at 250" theme of Week Six! You'll not only learn the basics of chocolate and major changes to the chocolate industry since 1776, you'll also sample some of the top dessert preferences of our U.S. presidents through the vehicle of gourmet Belgian chocolate-based fudge! This single day course is being offered on Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday.

classes.title: Chocolate Tasting Around the World
classes.description: The best chocolate in the world is simply the one you enjoy most. Join us on a journey to broaden your palate as we introduce you to fine chocolates from around the world. Using your senses of sight, smell, touch, and taste, we will evaluate over 16 chocolate samples to find the one that leaves you wanting more. Explore the fascinating history of chocolate, examine the complexities of cacao cultivation, and learn how chocolate makers create their delicious bars. Examine the ethical sourcing of chocolate and discuss the future of chocolate production in society today and tomorrow.

classes.title: A Changemaking Chef's 2026 Dinner Table
classes.description: Five lectures re-imagine a novel way of bringing meals to the table, employing foods and processes that sustain agriculture/farming practices; utilizing 21st century biological science which supports the growth of a diverse microbiome, a gold standard for sustaining health; promoting a culture of wellness within the family; perpetuating biochemical stability in those at the table; and expanding our resilience so as to increase the quality of our lives while enjoying the gastronomy of the meal.

classes.title: If Chocolate Brings You Joy: Friday Session
classes.description: As Chautauqua explores food systems and gathering during Weeks 8 and 9, chocolatier Jill Sandler will discuss the fragility of cacao, the creation of chocolate, and how one can incorporate whimsy and fun into chocolate flavors, structures, and gatherings. Students will enjoy substantial samples of Jill's gourmet Belgian chocolate-based treats. This single day course is being offered on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

classes.title: Is it worth it? Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Sauvignon Edition
classes.description: This is one of Sam Whitmore's favorite classes to teach. Most people have a preconceived idea that higher price equals higher quality, that is not always the case. This blind tasting class will challenge your palate to try and decipher which wine costs more ranging from $15 up to $80. The wines will include three each of Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Sauvignon. After tasting through all the wines, we will reveal the wines and price, then discuss what goes into the price of a given wine. It is harder than you think! Each of the six wine selections consists of an approximately 2-ounce pour.

classes.title: Understanding Food and Wine Pairing
classes.description: We will taste and discuss six wines; each paired with an appetizer designed to complement the wine. We will try a Champagne, French Chardonnay, California Chardonnay, Sangiovese, Pinot Noir, and Cabernet Sauvignon.

classes.title: Lessons from a Showgirl: The Empowering Lyrics of Taylor Swift
classes.description: Calling all Swifties and those curious about Taylor Swift's lyrics. Taylor's songs of conquering her own personal challenges and overcoming adversity and renewed strength have resonated deeply with millions. In this course, we'll examine selected songs and take a deep dive into the lyrics from her twelve albums. We will discuss the stories behind the songs and then consider what the song means to us personally. A journal and Swiftie friendship bracelets will be provided!

classes.title: Building Capacity for Racial Understanding
classes.description: Women of Color (African, Asian, Latinx) have endured through trauma and oppression, both physical and emotional, YET, "Still We Rise". Applying the principles of the Cultural Congruence Pyramid© to build capacity, we will experience an insightful examination of our implicit and explicit racial and gender beliefs, attitudes, and biases. Their unknown stories will influence and inspire. Music, visual arts, and illustrations will enhance our examinations via video clips and children's books.

classes.title: Exploring the Imposter Phenomenon: A Workshop on Self-Trust, Belonging, and Confidence
classes.description: Even the most accomplished among us sometimes feel undeserving of our success or worry we'll be "found out." This engaging workshop explores the Impostor Phenomenon, that quiet voice of self-doubt that can hold us back from joy and confidence. Through conversation, reflection, and simple evidence-based strategies, participants will learn to identify internal narratives, reconnect with personal strengths, and root themselves in authenticity and self-trust.

classes.title: Remembering with Love: A Workshop on Grief and Joy
classes.description: Life at Chautauqua is filled with joy, tradition, and community. And yet many of us carry private griefs into this sacred space. This one-day workshop offers a gentle, supportive environment to honor loved ones while embracing the renewal of Chautauqua. Through reflection, conversation, and simple creative exercises, we'll explore how memory, community, and joy can coexist. No experience required, just a willingness to notice, share, and connect with others who understand that love and loss often walk together.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Wider Spheres of Consciousness
classes.instructor: Krista Stanley, Ph.D. & Edwin Olson, PhD
classes.description: With our narrow bandwidth of perception, we humans miss the wide range of information that is available from the intelligence and creativity of our conscious universe. The new sciences now recognize the value of our subjective experiences to understand the fullness of reality. In this course we will concentrate on the post-materialist understanding of reality and explore our capacity to link with the subtle streams of information "beyond the brain".

classes.title: Carry the Spirit of CHQ Home
classes.description: How will you carry the spirit of CHQ home? After a week of powerful experiences and conversations, this interactive session helps you turn insights into action. Reflect on what moved you most, prioritize what matters, and build a personalized plan to carry the CHQ spirit into your everyday life, long after you've left the grounds. This single day course is being offered on Thursday and Friday.

classes.title: Gazing Inward and Outward: Connecting Mindfulness and Civic-Mindedness in Complex Times
classes.description: In this course, participants will explore how mindfulness can be leveraged to support productive civil discourse and meaningful civic life. We will delve into "civic-mindfulness" to consider how our thoughts are shaped by aspects of society that are apparent, and by more nuanced social forces. Participants will engage in contemplative practices, insightful mini-lectures, and lively discussions as we investigate our "full humanness" as citizens in a world that is complex, beautiful, and rife with contradictions.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Beyond Us vs. Them: How to Bridge Divides and Build Connection
classes.description: In a polarized time of misunderstanding and mistrust, this course will help you learn how to bridge divides. Drawing from psychology, conflict resolution, and real-world dialogue practices, we will learn to recognize and navigate identity-based conflict, cultivate empathy and curiosity across differences, engage in constructive conversations with disagreeable people, and build communities grounded in mutual respect. Through interactive exercises, case studies, and personal reflection, you will leave with practical tools to foster understanding and lead change in the workplace, congregation, classroom, neighborhood, or family.

classes.title: How to Talk When We Disagree
classes.description: In a time of deep division, discover how curiosity is a civic superpower that can bridge divides. This interactive course invites Chautauquans to practice courageous conversations across political and social differences. Through guided dialogue, reflection, and empathetic listening, participants will explore tools to rehumanize others, foster connection, and navigate disagreement with openness, drawing inspiration from Monica Guzmán's transformative approach to civic curiosity.

classes.title: Understanding Personal Fraud
classes.description: Do you worry that someday you may become a victim of personal fraud? Is personal fraud on the rise? Each year the FBI receives thousands of fraud complaints. In the last reporting year almost 850,000 complaints were received. The related complaints represented $16.6 billion in actual losses, which is a 33% increase over the previous year. In this class, we will examine some of the more common types of personal fraud, preventive measures to deter fraud, and steps to take if you are a victim of personal fraud.

classes.title: Meaning by Doing: What's Fulfilling and Why
classes.description: Insights from philosophy, theology, and psychology reveal how action can produce meaning. But what underlying drives motivate our actions? Drawing on "Wellsprings of Work: Surprising Sources of Meaning and Motivation", this class explores a dozen drives operating beneath the surface of daily life that motivate and create meaning, from young adulthood through middle age into retirement, along with a workbook for applying these drives in your own life.

classes.title: Become a Feedback Ninja
classes.description: Feedback drives improvement in every context: family, community and professional, but most of us avoid giving it until problems escalate. Through hands-on exercises and real-world practice, this interactive session provides a practical framework for delivering timely, clear, and constructive feedback. You'll learn to address issues as they arise without triggering defensiveness, stop postponing difficult conversations, and transform feedback from an awkward obligation into a genuine relationship strengthener. Expect an active, playful session, not a lecture.

classes.title: I'm Still Here: Redefining Your Purpose After the Loss of a Spouse
classes.description: You've lost your person. The silence is loud, the nights are long, and the question "Now what?" looms large. I Am Still Here is a gently humorous, deeply compassionate guide for widows and widowers navigating life after loss. With stories, prompts, and a few well-earned laughs, we'll explore how to live on when half your heart is gone. This course won't rush you through grief but it will help you rediscover your voice, your identity, and maybe even your sense of humor. Because if you're still breathing, you still matter.

classes.title: Thou Shalt Not Be Bamboozled: A Senior's Guide to Outsmarting Scammers
classes.description: Let's face it, scammers are getting smarter, sneakier, and better at pretending to be someone they're not. Whether it's a fake charity, a too-good-to-be-true offer, or a "grandchild" needing bail money, today's fraudsters know exactly how to push your buttons. Thou Shalt Not Be Bamboozled is a practical, often hilarious, guide to sniffing out scams and staying one step ahead. You'll learn to spot the red flags, protect your assets, and guard your trust like the treasure it is. Because wisdom doesn't age, and neither does your right to peace of mind.

classes.title: ADHD: Navigating the Education System
classes.description: This course empowers parents with practical tools to advocate for children who struggle with focus. Learn about ADHD types, strengths, and school-based challenges. Then explore Tier 1–3 supports and what to do when your child is struggling. Gain a clear understanding of the referral and testing process including rating scales, cognitive and academic assessments. Finally, learn how eligibility is determined and compare 504 plans versus IEPs with an overview of the IEP format.

classes.title: Discovering and Leveraging Your Strengths
classes.description: What happens when you lead with what's right about you? Through the Gallup CliftonStrengths® assessment and guided reflection, participants will uncover their top strengths and learn to apply them in daily life, relationships, and leadership. This interactive seminar blends self-discovery, discussion, and practical exercises to help you transform natural talents into tools for fulfillment, balance, and purpose so you can live and work from your strengths every day.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Navigating IEPs
classes.description: Navigating IEPs Class empowers parents to confidently navigate the IEP process. This course explains eligibility, referrals, timelines, and the annual review with the case manager. Parents learn to understand Present Levels of Performance, Special Factors, and FBA/BIP. The class reviews how to assess needs, evaluate past goals, and develop new ones. It concludes with a clear overview of program summaries, accommodations, services, testing requirements, and placement options equipping families to advocate effectively.

classes.title: Communicate Across Generations: Talking to Your Grandkids
classes.description: This discussion-based workshop explores how communication styles shift across generations. We'll look at the basics of child and adolescent development, changing cultural norms, and how curiosity can build connection. Through real-life scenarios and role play, participants will practice ways to ask questions, share experiences, and stay involved. Along the way, we'll touch on digital etiquette, strategies for meaningful conversation, and the value of modeling rather than instilling.

classes.title: The Out-of-Sync Child: Understanding Kids with Sensory Challenges
classes.description: About 16% of schoolchildren have Sensory Processing Differences (SPD) that cause the children's unusual responses to ordinary sensations and hinder their development. These "out-of-sync" children are bewildered by their world, as well as bewildering to their grownups. This course explains why some kids strive to get or get away from certain sensory stimuli; provides parenting and teaching strategies to improve home and school life; and offers sensory-motor activities to help children get in sync.

classes.title: Manage Stress, Anxiety, Fear, and Worry
classes.description: A practical workshop that teaches simple strategies to manage daily stress, anxiety, fear, and worry. Participants learn why these reactions happen, how to spot triggers, and how to use easy evidence-backed techniques to calm the nervous system and regain perspective. This course offers hands-on practice and tools so that participants build a personalized calming toolkit and create small, steady habits that bring more balance, fulfillment, and peace into daily life.

classes.title: Personalized Resilience for Midlife & Beyond
classes.description: Boost your resilience and thrive. Join Eileen Caroscio, co-author of Midlife New Life: Living Consciously in Midlife and Beyond as she guides you through creating a personalized Resilience Plan for navigating life's challenges and opportunities. You'll receive actionable tools, worksheets and key mindsets to enhance your adaptability, creativity and well-being. Engaging discussions will add wisdom and clarify your insights. This class will appeal to anyone designing a resilient and intentional life.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Express Yourself Authentically with Intention and Impact
classes.description: How do delivery and personal interactions affect your response? This course of discovery will provide tools to create a positive impact, enhancing your in-person and online presence. Using innovative strategies, we will explore the elements of appearance, voice, cadence, attitude, gestures, protocols, and techniques for Zoom appeal. You can benefit from exchanges, practice scenarios, and constructive coaching with participant feedback in a supportive environment to increase credibility, and confidence and expand your effectiveness in multiple settings.

classes.title: Four Days of Thanks Gratitude Workshop
classes.description: Over four days, this intimate workshop helps participants rediscover the grounding power of gratitude. Through guided journaling, reflective conversation, and individual writing projects, students will create a gratitude journal, write a thank-you note to someone who had a positive impact on their life, and develop a tribute to someone they miss or hope to reconnect with. Together, we'll explore how gratitude clarifies what matters, strengthens relationships, and opens space for healing and renewed connection.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Bringing the Medicine Wheel to Life
classes.description: We will gather together to explore the Native American Medicine Wheel and to recognize its meaning and significance in our lives. Each participant will receive a pouch and seven stones to represent the sacred elements of the Medicine Wheel. Through the teachings of Twylah Nitsch, a Seneca wise woman, we will explore the unity of all existence as understood by indigenous people. We will find the areas where we are strongly involved or drawn to through curiosity. We will plan a future being in tune with nature and the Medicine Wheel.

classes.title: At the Intersections of Retirement, Purpose, and Aging
classes.description: What is it you plan to do with your one wild and precious life? asks the poet Mary Oliver. Are you anxious about retiring yet yearning to try new things, find greater fulfillment, and manifest your purpose in a different way? This interactive seminar is for those in a career transition phase who wish to engage in serious conversations about who they are and what they wish to do. Through discussion and self-reflection, participants will explore attitudes and obstacles, expand possibilities, and identify strategies for moving forward.

classes.title: C'mon, Get Happy: The Art of Practicing Gratitude
classes.description: Wondering how to up your happiness quotient? Practicing the art of gratitude is a proven way to plug into positivity and become more appreciative of the world around you. Explore simple yet effective ways to practice gratitude in your daily life and learn more about its beneficial effects on the body, mind, and soul. The class will feature interactive exercises and journaling to further tap into thankfulness, as well as a mindful labyrinth walk.

classes.title: Design Thinking in Action: Learn Creative Problem-Solving for Real-World Impact
classes.description: In this course, you'll identify a real-world challenge and experience firsthand how dynamic, energizing, and transformative creative problem-solving can be. Whether you address a pressing community issue or explore a personal topic like health and wellness, you'll craft imaginative solutions with real impact. Working in small teams (you will be matched with others based on your "superpower"), you'll journey from defining a meaningful problem to developing a smart, innovative solution ready for the world.

classes.title: Service Dog, Therapy Dog, or Emotional Support Dog
classes.description: This course offers a brief, practical introduction to service dogs, therapy dogs, and emotional support animals, with a focus on the laws that govern their training and public access. Students will learn the key differences among these categories, the legal standards that apply to each, and the common misconceptions surrounding online registrations and certifications. The course also addresses essential questions for individuals, housing providers, and business owners regarding rights and responsibilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act and related regulations.

classes.title: Creative Courage: Finding Opportunity in Chaotic Times
classes.description: You are invited to a spacious, transformative journey into navigating uncertainty with clarity, imagination, and heart. Using coaching practices and wellness tools, this four-day workshop helps you transform challenge into creative possibility, decode chaos, reclaim agency, and uncover emerging opportunities. You'll leave equipped to lead yourself and others with grounded confidence and inspired insight.

classes.title: Next Steps in Your Anti-Racism Journey
classes.description: How much would it mean to put your values regarding racial equity into practice? During this interactive and introspective course, participants will explore the individual and systemic threads of racism. The facilitators, one Black and one White, utilize a self-reflective approach through circle work, small groups, and pairs for increased engagement and transparency. This class involves looking at the impact of racism on all of us, how it shows up in systems, and how we can respond effectively by doing our own work. We will focus on ally-ship as action-oriented rather than a static identity.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Stepping Stones: A Shift in Perspective
classes.description: What if you could live a more present, curious, and joyful life! Learn to trust yourself, be more understanding of your motivation, clarify your purpose. Embrace the Four Stepping Stones: Create Sanctuary (be safe in your environment), Cultivate Gratitude (live a life that reflects appreciation and navigates through fear), Manifest Grace (recognize moments of Oneness), and Allow Mercy and Forgiveness (for yourself and then others) in your life.

classes.title: The Royals Who Formerly Owned the Stolen Louvre Gems
classes.description: Discover when and where the former owners of the stolen Louvre gems lived. Learn about the two queens, two empresses, and two princesses who formerly wore the dazzling crown jewels. Were the brilliant gems their private possessions or were they owned by the state? Hear about American connections!

classes.title: Our Most Contentious Presidential Elections
classes.description: So, they say that since 2016, the presidential elections were the most contentious in American history. Hardly! The class will focus on several of the most controversial elections over our first 200+ years. Some of America's most seminal presidents were involved in brutal elections. This will be a timely opportunity for you to review election history in advance of both the upcoming midterms and the rapidly approaching next presidential campaign.

classes.title: Women Justices of the Supreme Court
classes.description: Six remarkable women have served on the Supreme Court in the last 45 years, changing the face of the Supreme Court and influencing the course of American law. Women now outnumber men in attending law schools. We'll discuss the accomplishments, ideas, and stories of these fascinating six women jurists and evaluate their legacies and contributions.

classes.title: WWII's Double V: Victory Against Fascism and Racism
classes.description: World War II was a pivotal time for the US, including historically marginalized groups. Learn about Double V: Victory Against Fascism Abroad and Racism at Home, its history and resulting legacy. From the Tuskegee Airmen, Triple Nickels, 6888th Postal Battalion and other Black units, to Code Talkers, WASP, Aztec Eagles, and other historically segregated groups, RISE ABOVE Ambassador Chelle Lewis and Cherokee National Treasure and Code Talker Descendent Robert Lewis will share little known history and dispel common misconceptions in this interactive workshop.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Lincoln and The Media: Things They Never Taught You
classes.description: Media plays a central role in modern lives, but this is nothing new. It has always been an important part of our history. During the Civil War, America's most existential crisis, President Lincoln both masterfully dealt with the newspapers while also being the most vilified man in America. He shut down many "disloyal" newspapers and jailed hundreds of editors. The class will evaluate that history, the First Amendment, and related Civil Liberties in wartime.

classes.title: The Art of Democratic Engagement: Practicing Effective Advocacy as America Turns 250
classes.description: In an era defined by polarization, distrust of institutions, and political gridlock, many Americans feel powerless to influence elected officials or shape public policy. In this course, participants will learn how to influence public policy, communicate effectively with elected officials, and build bipartisan relationships even in contentious times. Taught by a former congressional staffer and government affairs leader, the class blends behind-the-scenes insights from Capitol Hill with practical tools for advocacy.

classes.title: Dying To Get In: American Cemeteries in the Nineteenth Century
classes.description: This interactive lecture class will examine the history of cemeteries in the 19th century through their landscape design, gravestones and artwork, epitaphs, and people. We'll explore the evolution of the Rural Cemetery Movement and the ways cemeteries transformed from graveyards for the dead into places designed for people to visit as green spaces, places of commemoration, and amass collective memory.

classes.title: Free Speech in America at 250
classes.description: Freedom of the press and freedom of speech are among our most beloved constitutional rights, but they have come under pressure in the last few years. We'll review how the Supreme Court has shaped free speech in America over 250 years and we'll discuss how our courts are currently dealing with threats to free speech and freedom of the press.

classes.title: America in the 1950s
classes.description: This course will examine the United States during the 1950s, with consideration of the political, social, and cultural context. The 1950s left a conflicted legacy, often portrayed in the popular culture as prosperous "Happy Days" of suburban bliss yet subject to revisionist accusations of Cold War hysteria, conformity, and a stifling "feminine mystique." Our exploration will examine events, phenomena, and personages as diverse as Ike, McCarthyism, Marilyn Monroe, television's ascendancy, and the Montgomery bus boycott.

classes.title: Making Sense of the Supreme Court: 2026 Edition
classes.description: By June 2026, the Supreme Court will have addressed many legal challenges arising from Executive Orders and other political controversies. What do the justices have to say about the use of presidential power? What legal rationales support their 2026 decisions? We'll discuss the most significant decisions of 2026 and evaluate the Supreme Court's role in protecting our 250-year-old democracy.

classes.title: Lobbying: The Grease That Makes the Legislative Process Work or the Great Corrupter
classes.description: Aaron Kaufman, a member of the MD House of Delegates will discuss being lobbied, its benefits and detriments. Aaron also works as a registered lobbyist on Capitol Hill, where he lobbies on the federal level. He will bring his expertise and knowledge as a state Delegate and as a federal lobbyist to lift the curtain to reveal and explain the lobbying process. Joshua Kaufman is an attorney. He will discuss the history of lobbying, its legal and ethical concerns and highlight scandals. Case studies on the role of lobbyists will be presented, with video interviews with other lobbyists.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Fascism: Can it Happen Here?
classes.description: In the 1930's author Sinclair Lewis wrote a dystopian novel, "It Can't Happen Here," about fascism coming to America. The rise of fascism has been one of the most destructive movements of the past hundred years, bringing oppression, war and devastation in its path. In this three-session course, the first hour will seek to define what fascism is based on its characteristics. The second hour will review the historical experience of fascism and why it has appealed to many despite historical failures. The third hour will compare the political events in contemporary America with historical fascism.

classes.title: The Phenomenon of Hitler and the Third Reich
classes.description: How could Germany, a nation renowned for its level of education, culture and scientific achievement fall under the spell of Adolf Hitler? He was a complete unknown in 1919 but rose to power in a modern nation by 1933 and initiated the most destructive war in history. How could this happen? The essence of this course will be to explore the answers to these questions. It will show how a democracy was replaced by an authoritarian regime and the inevitable result of maniacal power without limit.

classes.title: Appalachian History and Culture
classes.description: What and where is Appalachia, and how has its history shaped the region's values? Once one of the most independent and prosperous parts of the country, it is now among the most economically challenged. Even so, its language, literature, crafts, and cultural values continue to influence the nation in powerful ways. This course offers an introduction to the richness and complexity of Appalachian life and is designed to spark your curiosity for all things Appalachian.

classes.title: U.S. Presidential History: Assassination and Attempts on our Presidents
classes.description: This class provides an overview of successful and attempted presidential assassinations, focusing on political motives, security failures, and national consequences. Students engage with historical case studies to understand how these events reshaped presidential protection and influenced public perceptions of leadership.

classes.title: U.S. Presidential History: Ranking of Presidents from Greatest to Worst
classes.description: This class reviews major scholarly approaches to ranking U.S. presidents, including criteria such as leadership, crisis management, and policy impact. Students compare historical and contemporary evaluations and participate in guided discussion to consider how presidential legacies are constructed and contested.

classes.title: U.S. Presidential History: The Great Scandals of Our Presidents
classes.description: This class analyzes major presidential scandals from the early republic to the modern era. Students explore the political, legal, and cultural implications of these controversies and discuss how scandal shapes public expectations of executive behavior. Interactive dialogue encourages evaluation of accountability and ethics in the presidency.

classes.title: U.S. Presidential History: The Health Secrets of the Presidents
classes.description: This class examines the medical histories of U.S. presidents and the ways in which health, illness, and secrecy have affected leadership and governance. Students consider historical examples, ethical questions, and the impact of presidential health on national stability. Open discussion encourages critical reflection on transparency and public trust.

classes.title: Democracy in Crisis
classes.description: Democracy is in recession. The optimism of the Arab Spring and the belief in liberal democracy's inevitability have faded. Today, media-driven virtual realities distort public opinion and weaken civic discourse. This course examines the roots of the current democratic crisis—across political perspectives—and explores ways to restore more deliberative, constructive democratic practices. Robert Cavalier specializes in deliberative democracy and has led projects on deliberative polling and democratic dialogue nationwide. His books include Democracy for Beginners (2009) and Approaching Deliberative Democracy: Theory and Practice (2011).

classes.title: U.S. Presidential History: The Impactful First Ladies
classes.description: This class examines the evolving public and political roles of First Ladies in the United States. Emphasis is placed on their influence on policy, social reform, and national identity. Through interactive discussion, students analyze how these women shaped presidential administrations and contributed to broader cultural change.

classes.title: The Vietnam War Era Through Music and Movies
classes.description: Using recorded and filmed examples of music, movies, TV and documentaries from the Vietnam War era (especially 1963–1975) the class will explore interactions between social, political, cultural, and military factors. We will address how popular music changed during (and because of) the war, and how media makers and commentators interpreted developments in Vietnam. Numerous music videos and selected movie videos from the era will be played. There will be discussion time included each day.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: Conspiracy Theories in America
classes.description: This course will examine conspiracy theories in the United States. First, we will explore the personality traits, emotional states, cognitive styles, and social motivations that are associated with a tendency to believe in conspiracy theories. Next, we will analyze a handful of conspiracy theories surrounding the Kennedy assassination, 9/11 and the New World Order. Lastly, we will acquire the tools needed to steer clear of the conspiratorial rabbit holes we may encounter in our own lives.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: Chautauqua and the Art of the Book: A Loving History
classes.description: From its founding to the present day, Chautauqua has had a unique and influential relationship with lifelong reading and the treasuring of literature. Less well known is its relationship with the hands-on creativity of the Art of the Book as a studio practice. This course introduces some Chautauquans of the 20th Century Arts and Crafts and the so-called "Book Beautiful" movement including Ellen Gates Starr and Addie Mae Smith Wilkes, linking the excitement generated by their contributions to the high value Chautauqua Institution upholds regarding writers and readers today.

classes.title: Films in Times of Peril and Hope: Powell and Pressburger
classes.description: From 1939 through 1946, Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger made 8 engaging and provocative films in London while war was outside the studio. They depicted lived experiences of audiences facing ongoing peril. Their audiences loved what they saw then, and today they are numbered among the BFI Top 100 British Films. We will spend extended time with each film to find the context and meaning which was placed with deliberate and deliberately subtle artistic intent. We will discover how war, culture and new literature shaped, and redefined what it means to live through time of danger.

classes.title: Chile: From Democracy to Dictatorship and Back Again
classes.description: How did Latin America's most stable democracy plunge into 17 years of brutal dictatorship? This course looks at late 20th century Chile: the election of Socialist President Salvador Allende; the legacy of his reforms; the resistance of the political Right and foreign governments; and the subsequent military coup of Sept 11, 1973. The experiences of the detained, tortured, exiled, and disappeared will reveal General Pinochet's brutality and oppression. Parallels will be drawn to current events, especially regarding immigration, US intervention, and threats to democracy.

classes.title: Walking the Crusades
classes.description: Come walk Palestine Park and learn the history of the Crusades! In the centuries following Pope Urban II's 1095 call for a crusade to the Holy Land, hundreds of thousands of Europeans journeyed to the Levant to participate in this invasion and colonization effort. Join me at Palestine Park as to assess the geographic and political history of the crusading era, focusing on the first Crusade, Crusader Kingdoms, and Saladin's reconquest in the twelfth century.

classes.title: When Should Courts Impose Restraints on Presidential Power
classes.description: The Supreme Court has rarely been called upon to restrain Presidential power and even more rarely during peace time. But the current President has ruled as never before by Executive Order without Congressional authorization or with questionable interpretation of Congressional statutes. Under what circumstances should the Supreme Court impose restraints on the President to do so?

classes.title: Understanding the U.S. Constitution: What it says and What it means
classes.description: This 5-day course explores the origins and foundational principles of the U.S. Constitution. Students will analyze the influence of Enlightenment philosophers (Locke, Montesquieu) and historical documents (Magna Carta, Mayflower Compact). The curriculum covers the inadequacies of the Articles of Confederation and examines the Constitutional Convention debates, major compromises, and core principles like federalism and the separation of powers, culminating in the ratification debate and the addition of the Bill of Rights.

classes.title: Baseball Couples: Odd and Others
classes.description: Major League Baseball is celebrating its 150th birthday in 2026. The game has been populated by a variety of fascinating couples who have added to its rich history. The class explores a variety of baseball couples, among them manager-player couples John McGraw & Christy Mathewson, Frankie Frisch and Dizzy Dean, Casey Stengel and Yogi Berra, Earl Weaver and Jim Palmer. We will also explore the baseball couple who had major impact in racial desegregation off the field as well as on the field, Branch Rickey and Jackie Robinson. Baseball couples in literature and the arts will also be discussed.

classes.title: The Separation of Church and State
classes.description: How much separation of church and state has there been in our history, and how much do we really want? Are the two religion clauses in the First Amendment complementary or contradictory? What was the original understanding of their meaning and when was it first applied to the states? How should they apply now to the right of a web designer to refuse to serve same-sex weddings, to a corporate rejection of Affordable Act requirements regarding contraception, and to states issuing vouchers that can be used for K-12 religious education?

classes.title: American Voices: Stories from our Nation
classes.description: As our nation marks its 250th anniversary, this course highlights the stories and legends that have shaped America. Through daily storytelling, read-alouds, and discussion, we will explore four sub-topics: Immigrant Voices (stories of those who came to America seeking a better life); The Stories Behind the Songs (origins of our patriotic tunes); Unsung Heroes (everyday people who strengthened our nation); and Remember the Ladies (women who made significant contributions throughout American history).

classes.title: Political Philosophy in Uncertain Times
classes.description: Today, uncertainty in many countries results from globalization that increases vulnerability to other countries and reduces traditional employment; electronic technologies used to erode trust in people and institutions, thereby reducing civic engagement and increasing social isolation; changes in moral norms; the pressures of immigration; and climate change and species extinction. This course considers responses based on alternative political philosophies, such as authoritarianism, nationalism, libertarianism, free-market conservatism, utilitarianism, and social contract theory.

classes.title: WWII, the Holocaust, & the Nuremberg Trials
classes.description: World War II was the most cataclysmic event in modern history, and its reverberations are still being felt 80 years later. Come learn about the war, how it spawned the Holocaust, and how America led the drive to punish the Nazi perpetrators.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: President Lincoln's Cottage presents Prison Reimagined: America 250
classes.description: While living at the Cottage, President Lincoln made some of his most lasting decisions about freedom, citizenship, and the nation's future. In December 2026, Prison Reimagined: America 250, an art exhibition comprised entirely of pieces created and curated by incarcerated artists, is set to debut at President Lincoln's Cottage. The artists make meaning of America's semiquincentennial based on their experience as Americans who have lived within and navigated the carceral system. Each session will feature a visual or written work from the exhibit that the group will examine together. There will be a display of a small sampling of artwork from the forthcoming exhibition for registrants to view. President Lincoln's Cottage will donate a portion of the proceeds from this session to the Committee of Incarcerated Artists and Writers.

classes.title: The Anglican Reformation: A 16th Century Clash of Religion and Politics in Europe
classes.description: This course surveys English history between the crownings of Henry VIII and James I. This period, generally known as the Anglican Reformation, importantly ended nearly 1,000 years of Catholicism in England. During the same period Anglicanism was born and fully developed. We will delve into the underlying historic, political, and social as well as theological development in England during these 94 years. The international intrigues which resulted from the religious turmoil in England will also be covered.

classes.title: Modern Legal Thought
classes.description: Is there a duty to follow an unjust law? Is religious freedom a free pass to violate the law? Should sex work be decriminalized? We'll examine these and other questions in the context of current events and the Supreme Court's recent decisions. We will discuss what the law is and what we think it should be. Come ready to learn about and respectfully discuss topics hotly debated in the news.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: The US and Europe from the end of the Cold War to Russia's Invasion of Ukraine
classes.description: When the Cold War ended, the relieved nations of the NATO alliance set about to build a new Europe "whole, free and at peace." These hopeful aspirations of the 1990s ran into obstacles including the Balkan Wars, the war on terrorism (including the "forever wars" in Afghanistan and Iraq), the rise of China, and finally, Russian President Vladimir Putin going to war to restore Russian influence in Europe. This course goes through those days from the post-Cold War years of hope to discussing how war returned to Europe and where do we go from here.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: Art, Symbolism, and Meaning in Cemetery Monuments
classes.description: Cemeteries are more than resting places; they are open-air museums filled with art, history, and coded language. This course examines the artistry and symbolism inscribed on cemetery monuments from the 18th century to the present day. Sharing examples of beautiful monuments within the United States, students will learn how to "read" gravestones as expressions of cultural values, personal identity, and changing attitudes toward death and remembrance. Topics include iconography and religious symbolism, the influence of artistic movements, and epitaphs as a form of storytelling.

classes.title: The Rural Cemetery Movement
classes.description: This course explores the origins, evolution, and cultural significance of the Rural Cemetery Movement in the United States during the 18th and 19th centuries, a transformative chapter in American urban planning, public health, and landscape design. Beginning with the austere burial practices of early America, we will trace how shifting ideas about death, health, and nature gave rise to a new vision of the cemetery as a place of beauty, reflection, and civic pride.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: A Conversation with Ken Burns
classes.description: Join Ken Burns for an in-depth conversation about his latest work, "The American Revolution." A filmmaker for almost 50 years, Burns will expand upon his morning lecture on the Amphitheater stage. An opportunity for Q & A, patrons can ask about Burns' awards, career, research and future plans.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: Colonial Williamsburg Foundation presents Nation Builders and Fifes & Drums Experience: Tuesday
classes.description: Lose yourself in the Spirit of '76! Hear the stirring sounds of Revolutionary War field music, courtesy of the Colonial Williamsburg Fifes & Drums. From recognizable names like Jefferson, Washington and Madison, meet the Nation Builders who helped shape their time and whose legacies continue to influence and inspire American ideals.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: Colonial Williamsburg Foundation presents Nation Builders and Fifes & Drums Experience: Wednesday
classes.description: Lose yourself in the Spirit of '76! Hear the stirring sounds of Revolutionary War field music, courtesy of the Colonial Williamsburg Fifes & Drums. From recognizable names like Jefferson, Washington and Madison, meet the Nation Builders who helped shape their time and whose legacies continue to influence and inspire American ideals.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: Colonial Williamsburg Foundation presents Nation Builders and Fifes & Drums Experience: Thursday
classes.description: Lose yourself in the Spirit of '76! Hear the stirring sounds of Revolutionary War field music, courtesy of the Colonial Williamsburg Fifes & Drums. From recognizable names like Jefferson, Washington and Madison, meet the Nation Builders who helped shape their time and whose legacies continue to influence and inspire American ideals.

classes.title: The Leader's Early Warning System
classes.description: Some leaders seem to sense trouble before it fully appears. This course will look at "early warning systems", habits of attention, questions, and listening that help us notice weak signals and act before problems escalate. Going deep into a real-world crisis case study, we'll study what the leaders saw, how they interpreted it, and how they responded. Through discussion and interactive exercises, participants will gain practical skills for sharpening their own awareness and navigate uncertainty with more confidence.

classes.title: Mary's World: The Time of the Annunciation
classes.description: The Virgin Mary has been an inspiration for more people than any other woman that ever lived. For Roman Catholics, Protestants, Jews, and Muslims, for artists, musicians, and writers everywhere, she has shown many faces and personified a variety of virtues. Learn about the world in her time!

classes.title: Women in the Bible
classes.description: Discover the extraordinary stories of women who shaped biblical history. In three dynamic sessions, we will explore a diverse cast of figures from queens and prophets to widows, servants, and leaders whose voices continue to resonate across the centuries. Our journey spans both the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament and the New Testament, featuring women such as Rebekah, Athaliah, the Queen of Sheba, the Israelite slave girl, Judith, Martha, Tabitha (Dorcas), and Phoebe. Each session highlights how their choices, courage, and faith influenced the unfolding story of God's people.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: The Big Three of Judaism
classes.description: God, Torah, and Israel are the three philosophical pillars upon which all of Judaism stands. What does Judaism teach about the Divine (God, angels, heaven and Jewish atheists) about the Bible (its origins, its contents and its authority) and Israel (the people, the land, and modern dilemmas about this). We will look at the different Jewish denominations on these three, ponder where we fit in, and also look broadly at where and whether Judaism and Christianity diverge or meet on these three foundational religious ideas.

classes.title: Introduction to Jewish Spirituality and Mysticism
classes.description: In these challenging times, we often try different ways to search for meaning, purpose, and sense in the world around us. We will look at a variety of sources, such as Torah, Midrash, Zohar, Mussar, and other Kabbalistic texts. We will also experiment with alternative experiences, such as guided meditation and chanting.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Thomas Merton: A Monk's Messages for Us Today
classes.description: Though cloistered behind monastery walls, Thomas Merton spoke prophetically to the world. Nearly six decades after his death, this Trappist monk's writings on environmental stewardship, racial justice, contemplative practice, and human interconnectedness remain strikingly relevant. This course explores Merton's enduring wisdom through discussion of carefully selected excerpts from his extensive body of work. We will consider how a man of silence had so much to say and why his messages matter now more than ever.

classes.title: Paradigms of Love: As Seen Through the Hebrew Bible
classes.description: This course will explore several paradigmatic Hebrew Bible couples, mining biblical text, exegesis, and modern music and literature to reveal the complex and multifarious contours of love and connection. Among others, this course will explore the relationship between Abraham and Sarah, Ruth and Boaz, and Esther and Xerxes/Mordecai. More than the stories of each of these couples, though, this course seeks to understand the nature and dynamics of the greatest force in the world: love.

classes.title: Popes' Art and Gorgeous Gardens at the Vatican
classes.description: Come explore the Papal Collection, the largest and most valuable art collection in the world. Spanning 27 centuries and displayed throughout lush gardens and 54 magnificent galleries in Vatican City, this collection includes Greek, Egyptian, Hebrew, Roman, Etruscan, Oceanic, African, Aztec, Muslim, Oriental, Impressionistic, and modern works. See the most dazzling art in the world!
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Sacred Ritual
classes.description: Rituals are all around us, some obvious (weddings, for example), some not so apparent (your morning routine, perhaps). Some rituals are intentional, and some accidental. Good ritual honors our personal story while simultaneously placing us into the bigger story of Life. In this course, we will explore the components of ritual and ceremony, and look at some of the rituals that have been meaningful in your life. We will look at the milestone moments in your life and you will have a chance to begin creating a ritual for one that is upcoming. Students may want to bring a laptop computer to class.

classes.title: Midrash: The Importance of the Story Behind the Story in Jewish Tradition
classes.description: In this course, popular CHQ instructor Rabbi Cookie Lea Olshein focuses on the power of Midrash (rabbinic stories interpreting Jewish sacred texts) as a way of better understanding traditional Jewish teachings. Studying both ancient and modern texts, as well as exploring examples of "visual midrash" via multiple modalities of Jewish artistic expression, helps us appreciate how learning "the story behind the story" often brings a deeper and more meaningful experience to traditional scripture-based study.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: Holistic Mental Health with Hildegard von Bingen
classes.description: A remarkable figure in medieval history, Hildegard of Bingen (1098–1179) was a German Benedictine nun, Christian mystic, visionary, healer, preacher, musician, composer, environmentalist, writer, language creator (lingua ignota), and advisor to many. This course explores how Hildegard's medieval holism examining all of a person's life for healing can be applied to modern day healing in mental health. Instructor will offer the particular lens of Austrian psychotherapist Alfred Adler's (1870–1937) holism in Individual Psychology as a useful comparison to Hildegard's practices.

classes.title: Flowers of the Bible: Their Meaning and Their Symbolism
classes.description: Biblical plants appear often in everyday language, and this class offers a fun way to explore the flora of the Bible as it shows up in art, medicine, and literature. You will also learn about the remarkable Swedish scientists Dr. Carolus Linnaeus and Dr. Frederik Hasselquist, the first to study and classify biblical botany. You may even be inspired to plant a biblical garden of your own.

classes.title: The Impact of the Hebrew Bible on the American Legal System
classes.description: Many people would be surprised how significantly the Hebrew Bible (particularly the Torah) has impacted our laws and how justice is pursued in America today. Taught by popular Chautauqua instructor Rabbi Cookie Lea Olshein, a practicing lawyer in Las Vegas before entering rabbinical school, this course covers the similarities and differences between ancient Jewish law and the structure of our modern legal system, discussing Jewish sacred texts, history, and how laws develop over time.

classes.title: Finding Grace: Compassion Meditations
classes.description: You are naturally empathetic; most humans and animals are. Studies show our brains even synchronize when we express compassion or help another. Although life experiences can cover this instinct, compassion can be strengthened to support greater happiness, optimism, reduced pain, and improve relationships. In this workshop, you'll learn the basic biology of empathy and two meditations, Metta and Naikan, that help deepen gratitude, connection, and balance perspective, supporting you to find peace and grace.

classes.title: The Neuroscience of Calm
classes.description: Your nervous system is designed to respond to life's challenges and bring peace. It doesn't always seem like that though. Learn the biology basics of how and why specific contemplative practices like breathing and kindness, shift the state of your mind and body into greater calm, connection, and presence. Join Dr. Annie Weisbrod, scientist, health coach, Buddhist teacher and author of one of the largest meditation studies published for this special experiential session.

classes.title: Religion/Spirituality and Health
classes.description: There is a relationship between an individual's participation in religious or spirituality activities and the quality of their health. This 3-session class will provide the best scientific information documenting the effect of religion/spirituality on mental and physical health and engage in discussion of interesting and unexplainable testimonies that suggest there may be something beyond our understanding. The information discussed will be applicable to all faiths. When we finish, do not anticipate any consensus other than that there is a relationship between religion/spirituality and health.

classes.title: A Guided Tour of Heaven: What the Bible tells Us
classes.description: This is not about near-death experiences. It is what the Bible says about how we get to heaven, our bodies in heaven, what we will do in heaven, even how eternity is different from time. Colossians 3: 2 "Think about the things of heaven, not the things of earth." (NLT) C.S. Lewis, "Christians who did most for the present world are just those who thought most of the next." Each attendee will receive the leader's 75-page book, "A Guided Tour of Heaven". Plan for this wonderful journey we all can take.

classes.title: Practicing Loving Thy Neighbor
classes.description: This interactive workshop is for anyone eager to add action to their "thoughts and prayers" for community healing. In our first two sessions, we will explore the issues we most want to tackle, the resources we have to offer, and the actions we can take to address those needs. We'll look at the journeys of everyday innovators who have stepped up around issues like homelessness, youth literacy, social alienation, religious disconnection, and more. In small groups, we'll discuss how each of us can move forward, independently or together, in our neighborhoods, congregations, nonprofits, and beyond to truly practice loving our neighbors. Our final session culminates in an Elevator Pitchfest where each participant presents an action plan for loving our neighbors and strengthening our communities.

classes.title: The Magic of Hebrew Letters
classes.description: Did you know that the word "Alphabet" actually comes from the first two Hebrew letters? Join us as we explore the significance and meaning of one of the world's oldest alphabets. Come learn stories and legends about the hidden meanings of each Hebrew letter's name, shape and numerical value. This class will not teach reading and no Hebrew reading or prior knowledge required.

classes.title: Exploring Spiritual Practices
classes.description: Find peace. Feel deeply. Free yourself from busyness by discovering spiritual practices that arise from your daily activities. Make your life more beautiful and meaningful by exploring spiritual practices that feed your soul. Bring a journal and an open mind to explore your inner life in ways that might surprise you.

classes.title: Guide for the Spiritually Lonely
classes.description: Millions today have no place to lay their heads from a spiritual or religious standpoint because the alternatives seem increasingly inadequate: atheism on one end; rabid right-wing ideology on the other. And in between, options that frequently ask adherents to leave their reasoning minds at the door, or that lead people to a kind of lonely, self-help approach to spirituality. In this course, we'll focus on key elements of religion and its context: "defanging" scripture; tracing mythological elements of Christianity; seeing God in new ways. We'll see if this leads us to a faith worth affirming.

classes.title: Not By Bread Alone: Judaism in Six Breads
classes.description: Holiday breads, Shabbat breads, Ashkenazi, Sephardi, Yemenite and Ethiopian breads, bagels and bialys and Jerusalem "bagelah" all tell the story of what it means to be Jewish, culturally, ethnically, and religiously. Taste history, discover the ways Jews have adapted to the culture in which they live while retaining unique traditions, and study the Biblical and Rabbinic texts which lend texture to the whole experience. Not a cooking class but a tasting class of 6–10 different kinds and categories of bread!

classes.title: Where Do We Go from Here: An Anti-Greed Gospel
classes.description: This course will explore the impact of greed in America through the lens of scripture, history, and economics. Built around the book, The Anti-Greed Gospel: Why the Love of Money is the Root of Racism and How the Church Can Create a New Way Forward by Malcolm Foley, the course will highlight the laws of the Torah and the teachings of Jesus, making the argument that we are called to care for one another materially.

classes.title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance - the Chautauqua Connection
classes.description: Early on in Pirsig's master work of modern philosophy he cites "a Chautauqua" as his mode of discourse, it being capable of deep as opposed to broad thought. In this class we will engage key Pirsig ideas culminating in his Metaphysics of Quality the new philosophy contribution displayed in this novel/memoir which has been compared to Moby Dick. We will read and discuss, perhaps engage in some difficult concepts of our own. Students should have read the book and perhaps its sequel, "Lila" before engaging.

classes.title: Human + AI: Skills for Thriving
classes.description: Explore human flourishing in a world where intelligence is shared with machines. Through hands-on experiments and intergenerational dialogue, this workshop-style course blends practical AI literacy with deep reflection on trust, creativity, ethics, and human agency. Confidently navigate when & how to use AI. Each session combines brief instruction with collaborative discussion, skill practice, and reflections on Human + AI partnership. You'll prompt an AI system to solve a real problem, examine its reasoning, identify its blind spots, then collaborate with classmates to improve the outcome.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: Science Ethics: Debating Moral Quandaries
classes.description: What can we learn from where science has "gone wrong"? History shows that scientists, like all people, are morally fallible. Through case studies and modern dilemmas, participants debate questions such as: Do ends ever justify means? How should we handle the intentional and unintentional consequences of discovery? The practice of science and how we apply its discoveries must be considered as separate ethical questions.

classes.title: Tech Tools to Make Organizing a Breeze
classes.description: Need to organize a big potluck dinner? Find a date for lunch with old colleagues? Help your condo's residents communicate? Build a simple website? Make nametags for a crowd? New technology tools make all of these tasks easier to do than in the past. The instructors will share tips about the web-based tools that they have discovered (many of them free of charge) to take care of these chores and organize groups of all sizes.

classes.title: Minds and Machines
classes.description: Can a machine possess a mind? Scholars from diverse fields have long debated this question. We will examine perspectives on artificial intelligence from philosophy, computer science, and literature. We will also discuss state of the art research from the field of cognitive neuroscience on consciousness. Throughout, we will consider the ethical implications of a world in which machines could someday have minds.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: Psychological Detectives: Media and Mind
classes.description: News sources are more numerous than ever, existing on multiple platforms, and ranging the full spectrum from low-quality fiction to high-quality objective reporting. Detecting the signal through the noise is a challenge. In this course we will sharpen our scientific critical thinking ability, playing the role of a psychological scientist investigating the impact of news and other media on thinking, reasoning, memory, and persuasion.

classes.title: Polymer Science for All Ages: Slime, Goop, and Other Creations
classes.description: This lively, family-friendly session brings chemistry to life through experiments with non-Newtonian fluids, DIY kinetic sand, and density challenges. Participants explore how everyday materials reveal molecular principles.

classes.title: Controversial Science: Evolution, Climate, and the Politics of Knowledge
classes.description: Why are evolution and climate science considered "controversial" in the United States despite overwhelming scientific consensus? This course explores the history of anti-science education tactics in the U.S., the social and political roots of science denial, and its practical consequences. Participants discuss strategies for bridging the gap between scientific consensus and public acceptance, emphasizing best practices to de-politicize science. A compelling case can still be made for the compatibility and coexistence of science and religion.

classes.title: Biomimicry: How Nature Inspires Human Innovation
classes.description: From Velcro to wind turbines, nature's designs inspire human problem-solving. This hands-on course introduces biomimicry through the AskNature design database and real-world case studies. Participants brainstorm and prototype sustainable innovations modeled on natural systems.

classes.title: Try AI Songwriting
classes.description: Whether you're a "traditional musician," lyricist/poet, or a total newbie wishing to do a first song for your partner (or pet), this class is for you: we'll run it like a one-room schoolhouse to accommodate anyone's level of expertise. Creators should bring a laptop to class and earbuds are a must. The last thirty minutes of each session will be a listening party where we share our work (if we like) and offer each other feedback (if requested). Everyone will leave with a small portfolio of finished songs. We'll also explore the ethical usage of AI.

classes.title: Curious Naturalists: Exploring the Diversity of Life on Earth
classes.description: Only about 10% of Earth's species have been identified. This course introduces taxonomy, phylogeny, and the joy of discovering and naming life. Explore how scientific naming fosters "biophilia," the innate human connection with living things. Retracing natural history through The Natural History of Chautauqua (McCaughey, 1917), participants revisit species recorded a century ago to see what has changed.

classes.title: AI for Personal Tasks & Problem Solving
classes.description: Explore AI through a personal lens; how everyday individuals can harness AI for their own needs, not corporate or professional applications. Our focus centers on four core capabilities: finding information efficiently, crafting personal writing, thinking through problems conversationally, and working with documents and materials you've gathered. Through live demonstrations, we'll introduce free versions of tools like Perplexity, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and NotebookLM, demonstrating real-world tasks you actually care about without getting lost in technical weeds.

classes.title: Guilty by Genetics
classes.description: For adults who know nothing about science, biology or genetics. With labs and problems, we'll have fun as we make edible DNA models with gumdrops and licorice, solve who licked the frosting off the back of the cake using genetic investigations, discuss ethical testing for conditions like Huntington's disease (e.g., Woody Guthrie), learn about principles demonstrated by calico cats, color blindness, hemophilia, viruses and bacteria, making protein from protein, even how to spell DNA!

classes.title: Climate Change: A Look at the Data
classes.description: A look at the data surrounding Climate Change or Global Warming. We will dive into what is going on and the likely drivers of our climate.

classes.title: Driving to Net Zero: Stories of Hope for a Carbon-Free Future
classes.description: Can you cut your fossil fuel use by 80% or more without sacrificing your lifestyle? Yes, and it's easier than you think! In this inspiring talk, David Hrivnak, author of Driving to Net Zero: Stories of Hope for a Carbon-Free Future, shares real-life stories of households powering their homes and cars with clean, emission-free energy. Learn how everyday choices can slash your carbon footprint while saving money and enhancing your life.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: Surviving AI in partnership with Arizona State University
classes.description: This event is a part of Chautauqua's partnership with Arizona State University and is hosted by comedian Shane Mauss and Athena Aktipis (featuring comedy, science & music.) Surviving AI is a comedy show that blends humor with thoughtful exploration of how humans relate to artificial intelligence and how we might build a more cooperative technological future. The evening begins with a stand-up comedy set, moves into a salon-style conversation with experts on AI and cooperation, and culminates in a live improvisational "battle" between a human artist and an AI, responding to each other in real time. Throughout the show, an LED screen displays dynamic visuals generated through human–AI collaboration, created live by AI artist Michael Strauss, inviting the audience to reflect on creativity, agency, and collaboration in an age of intelligent machines.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: The Science of Cooperation — How Understanding Our Evolutionary History Helps Us Build a Cooperative Future in partnership with Arizona State University
classes.description: Athena Aktipis, Associate Professor in the Department of Psychology at Arizona State University, Director of the Cooperative Futures Institute, The Interdisciplinary Cooperation Initiative, and The Cooperation Lab at ASU presents this compelling and timely Master Class. Athena's work focuses on cooperation and how it makes us stronger, more adaptable, and ready for an uncertain future.

classes.title: Electric Cars: Separating Hype, Deception and Facts
classes.description: Are electric vehicles (EVs) just overpriced toys with limited range and unreliable batteries? Do they strain the grid or harm the environment? Get the truth from David Hrivnak, an engineer and EV owner with 16 years of experience and over 275,000 gas-free miles. This engaging session cuts through myths and media noise, offering a clear, firsthand look at EV costs, performance, charging infrastructure, and environmental impact.

classes.title: Solar: Harnessing the World's Fastest Growing Energy Source
classes.description: Power outages whether from storms, cyberattacks, or grid failures, can disrupt modern life. Could solar energy be your solution? Join David Hrivnak, an engineer with over 80 residential and small industrial solar designs, to explore solar power, the world's fastest-growing energy source. This practical session covers everything you need to know to harness solar energy for your home or business.

classes.title: Impact of Climate Change on Alaska Native Communities
