classes.description: This course will describe the impact of the changing arctic environment on traditional Alaska Indigenous communities. These environmental changes include the disappearance of Arctic Sea ice, the decline of marine mammal and fish species, storm surges that erode entire coastal communities, the burning of millions of acres of tundra, and the melting of extensive permafrost. All these environmental changes affect key aspects of Inupiat culture: hunting, fishing, and gathering activities and the ethics involved in the extensive sharing of these resources.

classes.title: Engaging a Nuclear Proliferated World
classes.description: Utilizing the Manhattan Project as a primer, this five-lecture series explores the history of atomic weaponry from the advent of the atomic age; through the current nine or more members of the modern "nuclear weapons club" and into the future as to, recognizing the coming surge in nuclear proliferation, how America will engage and confront the numerous nation-states contemplating entry into this exclusive realm.

classes.title: Improving Our Transportation Fueling
classes.description: Conventional petroleum-based transportation fuels have undesirable impacts on health, the environment, and geopolitics. Advances in fuels and power/storage systems could lead to more sustainable alternatives. The course will summarize where we are, analyze past failures, and consider future options with an emphasis on electric propulsion systems. Bill Chamberlin will draw on his 30+ year participation in alternative fuels and engines to assess obstacles to consider in pursuing an environmentally sustainable transportation infrastructure.

classes.title: Fantastic Fungi
classes.description: Fungi have a huge impact on both humans and our planet. We will discuss how fungi were integral to the spiritual practices of the Ancient Greeks and the Incas. We will even find out about Beatrix Potter's first career as a mycologist. The class will learn about how fungi are now being used to build housing as well as break down plastics. The gardener in you will appreciate fungi for how they help nourish your plants. Lastly, we will look at current research that uses fungi to treat human illnesses such as anxiety and depression. This class will discuss all the fascinating aspects of fungi.

classes.title: How Local Ecology Drives Human Cultural Evolution: Lessons from Papua New Guinea
classes.description: How have environments shaped human culture and vice versa? Focusing on case studies from New Guinea, this course explores how geographic and ecological factors influence language, social structure, spirituality, and human-wildlife relationships. Participants will consider pathways from conflict to cooperation and the diverse meanings of "stewardship" across cultures.

classes.title: Sociobiology and the Science of Free Will
classes.description: Why do humans form tribes, create religions, and wage wars? Is between-group violence inevitable? Drawing on Robert Sapolsky's Behave and Determined, participants explore the biology and culture of morality, aggression, and cooperation. After an introduction to key principles, students anonymously "vote" before and after a structured small-group debate to assess how discussion and evidence influence beliefs about free will and responsibility.

classes.title: The Future of Investing: Innovation and Disruptive Technologies
classes.description: Discover how innovative and disruptive technologies continue to emerge and shape the future of investing. In this forward-looking class, we will explore groundbreaking trends in artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics and automation, autonomous vehicles, virtual and augmented reality and more. We will examine how these revolutionary technologies have the potential to redefine industries and create long-term investment opportunities. Join us to learn strategies for investing in tomorrow, today.

classes.title: Heir Conditioning: Making an Inheritance Mean Something
classes.description: An inheritance can launch your family to achieve greater accomplishments, or it can destroy their lives. Learn from actual case studies and specific techniques that will give meaning and significance to what you leave to your heirs. Create a legacy that will go on for generations, not used up in a year or less, using time-tested strategies. Let's make it mean something!

classes.title: Evaluating Continuing Care Retirement Communities
classes.description: Making the decision to move into a Continuing Care Retirement Community (CCRC) is a major financial and emotional decision. The typical CCRC allows an individual to age in place within a community campus. The standard model includes independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing care, and memory care. The move to a CCRC often involves a sizable entrance fee and an understanding of contracts, financial documents, and actuarial analyses. This course serves to aid in the decision-making process in order to help one to navigate through internal and external information.

classes.title: Investing in Megatrends and Beyond: How to Position Yourself
classes.description: The world of investing is rapidly changing year in and year out. To stay ahead, investors must identify the megatrends of tomorrow: artificial intelligence, quantum computing, blockchain technology, fintech, renewable energy, healthcare innovations, changes in demographics and more. This class blends practical investment ideas with market insights, helping students position their portfolio. Through clear explanations and real-world examples, students will gain tools to navigate change and make informed decisions aligning investments with emerging long-term trends.

classes.title: Deep Dive into Digital Marketing and Online Fundraising
classes.description: Ever wondered how to get more folks involved with a cause you care about? Interested in raising money online for your organization? Worried about building a robust email list or posting engaging content on social media? This is your chance to learn best practices for effective digital marketing and online fundraising from an industry leader. Several lucky participants will receive 1x1 coaching and the creation of custom strategy recommendations! This course is designed for both experienced and beginner digital marketers.

classes.title: Fundamentals of Bitcoin
classes.description: A non-technical introduction exploring the core principles of what Bitcoin is, how it works, and why it has value. Learn about wallets, how to send and receive Bitcoin, and the philosophical implications of this mysterious and new financial technology.

classes.title: Fixed-Income Investing
classes.description: Fixed-income investing can be a complex strategy for investors. This course will examine the pros and cons of investing in bond mutual funds and ETFs (exchange traded funds), and in individual bonds. We will learn about fixed-income markets and securities. This course will cover what I have learned in my 40+ years of fixed-income investing.

classes.title: Psyche and Eros: The Feminine Pathway
classes.description: A Jungian interpretation of this ancient Greek myth tells of a mortal princess who falls in love with the god of Love and must meet the jealous demands of his mother, the goddess Aphrodite (Venus). Psyche's story is our story as we navigate the journey towards individuation. Paradise lost and paradise regained are core human experiences explored with mythic metaphoric images.

classes.title: Emerson and Transcendentalism
classes.description: Explore highlights from Emerson's life and several of his essays including Self Reliance, The American Scholar, The Divinity School Address, etc. The Transcendentalist movement and its key players including Thoreau, Alcott, Margaret Fuller discussed. Topics such as slavery, rights of women, education reform and the Hudson River School movement included.

classes.title: Carl Jung's Red Book: A Further Exploration
classes.description: Following the 2025 class on the Red Book, this course will continue to explore the rich stories, visions and imaginings of the founder of Analytical Psychology. The book was written over 16 years after Jung experienced a mid-life crisis caused by his split with Freud. It is not necessary to have taken the 2025 class. Fascinating and spiritual!

classes.title: Joseph: Encountering Siblings
classes.description: Parental preference, youthful conceit, sibling envy, and dream interpretation are all aspects of this biblical story which will be studied psychologically for a depth of understanding. The story becomes our story in many ways as reconciliation, forgiveness, revenge, egotism, and love vs. power are encountered. Listen to this 3,000-year-old story again for the very first time.

classes.title: Jungian Psychology: Selected Topics
classes.description: Engage with such topics as: The sensate function, including a study of "The Lady and the Unicorn" tapestries; Is Joseph Cambell still relevant; Unconscious shadow energy in Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde; Goddess Fortuna: contemplating the human condition, etc.

classes.title: Dante's Divine Comedy: An Introduction
classes.description: As T. S. Eliot wrote: "Dante and Shakespeare divide the world between them – there is no third." Knowing the great works of literature must begin with Dante and his encounter with soul and divine mystery. This class will give an accessible overview of The Inferno, The Purgatorio and The Paradiso along with selected excerpts (with commentary) from each. Dante's life and exile from Florence discussed. Illustrations by Blake, Duer, Botticelli, and others included.

classes.title: Emily Dickinson: Ecstasy
classes.description: I find ecstasy in living; the mere sense of living is joy enough. For each ecstatic instant, we must an anguish pay. Dickinson explores her topics from multiple perspectives. Along with a study of selected poems, lecture material will place Dickinson in the context of her times with discussions on such contemporaries as Walt Whitman, Thoreau, Margaret Fuller and others.

classes.title: Masters Series Masterclass: Workshop. Engaging attendees using the Soul Boom Workbooks with Rainn Wilson
classes.description: Chautauqua Lecture Series keynote speaker Rainn Wilson hosts a workshop engaging the Chautauqua community with his journal-style Soul Boom Workbook: Spiritual Tools for Modern Living—written in collaboration with Wilson's SoulPancake co-founder and writer Shabnam Mogharabi. It is filled with hands-on prompts, inspired reflections, and ingenious creative activities. The session delves deeper into the indispensable companion book, based on his New York Times bestselling book—now a hit podcast—Soul Boom: Why We Need a Spiritual Revolution. Wilson's approach to spirituality is relatable and applies to people of all beliefs, even the skeptics. The journal enables readers to find more purpose, meaning, and spirituality in their hectic lives as they seek out practical and transformative answers to life's biggest questions. Wilson posits that a "Soul Boom" is the potential for a spiritual revolution to instigate transformations, both individually and collectively. It's the healing balm that our world needs in our contemporary mental health crisis.

classes.title: Psychological Perspectives on Envy
classes.description: Envy is a painful emotion (often unconscious) when another has something that is deemed desirable but unattainable. Unfavorable comparisons often lead one to angry responses. Studying envy through the lens of Jungian psychology results in a broader understanding of the human psyche and allows one to become savvier in navigating social landscapes. Historical and philosophical perspectives reviewed. Poetry, art, and excerpts from several films included.

classes.title: Cinema and Psyche
classes.description: Film excerpts will be used to study psychological issues in human relationships. The life of Tolstoy, one of the greatest writers who ever lived, will be discussed using film excerpts. He experienced a transformative life crisis and was overwhelmed with inner conflict in his elder years. Ordinary People will be revisited. Additional films discussed as time allows.

classes.title: Italy Off the Beaten Path
classes.description: You may know the touristy Italy; but there are many wonderful places away from the crowds. This class will introduce you to a half dozen spots that range from a little off the beaten path to way off. Come get inspired to visit more authentic parts of the country.

classes.title: Traveling in Italy
classes.description: Tips, Tricks and Traps for traveling independently in Italy. Day 1 covers logistics, including arriving, driving, trains, accommodations, money, and what you do and do not need for 220-volt electricity. Day 2 focuses on eating—gelato, coffee, restaurant menus, cooking, shopping, food trucks, and typical restaurant hours. Day 3 highlights fun activities such as beaches, museums, art, festivals, guides, and basic Italian language to help you get by.

classes.title: You Are Here: Adventures in Geography
classes.description: This short course offers an introduction to the joys of reading the landscape. Hands-on and interactive, we will explore some of the fundamental concepts and ideas of geography and apply them to our region and beyond. Google Earth on an iPad/tablet/laptop/smart phone will be helpful but not required.

classes.title: The Women who Shaped Us: Finding The Women in Your Family Tree
classes.description: This course will begin with an overview of the process of building a family tree and will highlight the problems associated with finding the women in your family history. Women are often absent from the historical record because they were prohibited from owning property, holding public office, voting or seeking higher education. Genealogists have discovered ways to find these hidden ancestors and these techniques are useful for finding other hidden ancestors.

classes.title: When Gentle Women Take a Stand
classes.description: What leads private people to take a public stance? The course begins with the experiences of two women who participated in a school desegregation workshop at Highlander Folk School in 1955, Rosa Parks and May Justus, a children's author. Their own words, found in interviews, speeches, and letters will tell the story. The course will culminate in a discussion of contemporary women of courage across fields (education, religion, the arts) and in our own lives.

classes.title: Don't You Forget About Me: "The Breakfast Club" 40 Years Later
classes.description: This course, based upon the 1985 film "The Breakfast Club" explores themes of identity, social pressure, and communication. The film's portrayal of students from diverse groups who spend a Saturday in detention with a resentful teacher, offers participants opportunities to reflect on and discuss their experiences in school and beyond. A workshop format, including film clips, songs analysis, and interactive activities acts as the jumping off point for these discussions. How well do the characterizations and plot hold up in a "6&7" world? With whom do you identify, or not?

classes.title: International Travel Tips and Tricks
classes.description: Whether or not you have traveled internationally, you will learn practical and money-saving tips from lessons learned by the instructor during her travel to over 100 countries on all seven continents, including scores of tours, cruises, expeditions, safaris, and independent explorations. Tips involve travel documents, health, comfort, avoiding crime, when and how to bargain, common errors with trip insurance, show and tell of useful items for international travel, and more.

classes.title: Japan 101: Touring Japan Like a Pro
classes.description: This course is for those interested in exploring Japan for the first time or for the first time after a long time away. We'll cover travel, including practical apps for journey planning; finding accommodations to fit budget and expectations; eating options for specific dietary needs; major tourist destinations and quieter alternatives; and planning a trip assuring safety and comfort while still leaving the door open for adventure.

classes.title: Canine Scent Work: The Nose Knows
classes.description: Want to exercise your dog physically and mentally while building your relationship? Come out and discover a fun way to channel your dog's natural sniffing talent! Scent games are an ideal way to stimulate your dog and can be done indoors or outdoors with dogs of all ages. Watch and learn as your dog detects an odor and hunts to locate its source. Have a good time while building skills through the week.

classes.title: How to Get Along with Your Adult Children: Even When You're Pretty Sure They're Wrong
classes.description: They're grown. They have opinions and somehow, you're still the one biting your tongue. "How to Get Along with Your Adult Children" is a warm, witty guide to keeping the peace (and your phone number unblocked) as your parent-child relationship evolves. With practical wisdom, a dash of humor, and zero lectures, this course helps you navigate role reversals, generational differences, and grandparenting boundaries without stepping on toes. It's about choosing connection over correction and love over "I told you so."

classes.title: Great Flying Stories
classes.description: Today it's drones and unpiloted urban mobility aircraft, but our grandparents remember the Wrights at Kitty Hawk, and flight defined the twentieth century. We celebrated aviation technology and the feats of pioneering aviators, and we ourselves began climbing aboard routinely. There have been first-rate writers among aviators. We will read very short stories and brief excerpts from longer works by authors who flew and wrote of flight and some famous fliers. We'll also screen clips from film adaptations.

classes.title: Chautauqua Film Intensive: Make a Short and Premiere It
classes.description: In five days, plan, shoot, and edit a well-made one-to-two minute short on your phone or camera. Then premiere it in a public showcase at week's end. Day 1 covers visual grammar and idea development. Day 2 focuses on framing, lighting, sound, and storyboards. Days 3 and 4 combine supervised shooting windows with in-room editing. Day 5 is the screening. Beginners welcome. Work entirely in class or take advantage of optional after-hours windows for pickups and polish.

classes.title: Environmental Ethics and Climate Change
classes.description: Whom does climate change harm most, and who should pay most to reduce its increasing threat? What are our energy alternatives? Is nuclear energy needed? Must we revise our transportation and residential infrastructures, reducing large semis on our roads and homes in flood-prone areas? Should environmental values guide our behavior as consumers, the kinds of cars and clothes we buy? Should environmentalists be vegetarians or vegans? The class discusses these and other matters at the intersection of climate change, modern life, and sustainability.

classes.title: Our National Parks: America's Best Idea in Crisis
classes.description: This course is an educational and outreach-focused event designed to deepen participants' understanding of the US National Parks' history, highlight current climate change risks, sustainability challenges, and empower them to champion the sustainability and stewardship of our parks. Participants will gain a comprehensive, visually engaging understanding of the national park system's history, challenges, and solutions. Additionally, attendees will leave with actionable outreach strategies and educational materials for community use.

classes.title: Why We Love Lucy: Her Life and Career
classes.description: Lucy's life and career from early days growing up in Celeron and Jamestown, her film career in the 1930s and 1940s, her innovations with Desi Arnaz in creating "I Love Lucy" and her later television series movie and projects. I will do a few "I Love Lucy" trivia questions at the end of each class and there will be a Lucy-related prize given away on the last day of the class. This will be from a drawing of names of the class participants and not based on trivia answers (that's just for fun!).

classes.title: Exploring Long Term Cultural Traditions
classes.description: Explore how long-lasting cultural movements grow in distinctive places, from the legacy of the Chautauqua Institution to the creativity of Burning Man. This course examines the shared practices, values, and identities that help ideologically rich communities endure over time. Through discussions on tradition, adaptation, and belonging, we'll uncover what enables place-based cultures to remain resilient and vibrant, offering insight into why certain gatherings continue to thrive across generations.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: Vintage Hitchcock: The Making of a Master
classes.description: Alfred Hitchcock was the Master of Suspense long before he came to America in 1939. He practically invented the British film industry in the 20s and 30s with such classics as The 39 Steps and The Lady Vanishes. We will view and discuss five of his finest films from this era. Each film will be introduced with an original video presentation, followed by an opportunity to share our reactions. And yes, the famous Hitchcock cameos begin with these movies.
classes.location: The Ida A. Vanderbeck Chapel Room

classes.title: LGBTQ+ Literature and Culture: Out in Nature
classes.description: From the poetry of Walt Whitman to Mary Oliver, to the essays and fiction of contemporary writers like Callum Angus, LGBTQ+ writers have drawn inspiration from nature and the natural world to express queer experience and to imagine queer futures. In this course we'll explore this relationship through short fiction and poems from selected writers. Through discussion and some short, focused writing, we'll draw upon the beautiful natural surroundings of Chautauqua to tease out how nature models queer transformations.
classes.location: Literary Arts Center at Alumni Hall

classes.title: College Football: Passion and Pageantry
classes.description: A look at the history of college football, from its origins and more than 150 years of evolution to the greatest teams, coaches, and players who shaped the sport. We'll explore the pageantry, passion, and rivalries that define the game and its devoted fans.
